When a group of European officials arrived in Kyiv to mark Ukraine’s Independence Day last month, they got some worrying news.

The European Union, a key backer, had earlier this year finalized a loan of more than $100 billion for the country. But Ukraine now faced an unexpectedly large defense budget shortfall, President Volodymyr Zelensky told allies. To get through the year, he would need $27 billion more.

Ukraine’s request surprised and unsettled many officials around Europe at a moment when Kyiv, short on air defenses to protect itself from nonstop Russian drone and missile attacks, faces one of its most dangerous moments since 2022.

Europeans understand Ukraine is in a fight for its existence but did not expect such a large budget shortfall, according to four European diplomats who, like others quoted in this piece, spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak publicly. In private, some have questioned whether money is being spent efficiently, two European officials said, or whether needs are being overstated.

Now, European officials are scrambling to understand where the shortfall came from, exactly how large it is and whether, or how, to send more money this year. Kyiv is also asking Britain, Canada and Japan to help cover the gap.

The surprise request threatens to complicate Ukraine’s relationship with allies at a moment it needs their support. The United States has stepped back from backing Kyiv financially, making European money more essential. But national leaders must balance their support for Ukraine with domestic spending priorities, or risk angering voters.

Kyiv’s shortfall also offers a stark reminder that the cost of backing Ukraine is on the rise. The nation faces relentless attacks from Russia, including strikes on ports that have deprived it of a major source of revenue. It is also critically low on U.S.-made interceptor missiles capable of shooting down ballistics, and is trying to scale up development of its own alternatives.

“The war has objectively become more expensive,” said Olena Prokopenko, a Ukrainian foreign policy specialist who is a senior fellow at the German Marshall Fund, a research institute.

She said that if Ukraine can show European nations that it truly needs the money, “I believe that they will find a way — for Ukraine’s sake, but also for their own sake.”

Where did the shortfall come from?

The source of the budget gap remains unclear and somewhat contested. Speaking in Kyiv last month, Mr. Zelensky said that some of the spending had happened under former defense minister Mykhailo Fedorov, who had advocated major changes in the defense industry and was recently fired in a move that sparked street protests.

The defense ministry “used funds that had been budgeted for the end of this year, and of course, the total gap is $27 billion,” Mr. Zelensky said at a meeting of European and British leaders on Aug. 24.

Mr. Fedorov has denied that such a large shortfall existed during his tenure and said it must be tied to projects under the ministry’s new leadership.

Ukraine has not yet publicized a full breakdown of its short-term budget needs, although Mr. Zelensky told journalists last month it includes weapons, soldiers’ salaries and family payments for soldiers killed in action.

Roksolana Pidlasa, head of Ukraine’s parliamentary budget committee, said she had been warned earlier this year that a shortfall of around $7.5 billion was expected. But military expenditures increased by more than 17 percent in the first eight months of 2026 compared with the year before, Ms. Pidlasa said.

“These gaps emerge because the war is just getting more and more expensive every year,” Ms. Pidlasa said. “We have to account for the fact that the Russian tactics change and it makes it worse for Ukraine.”

She said that the increase in Russian attacks on Ukrainian industry, including metallurgical plants and the grain export corridor, had lost Ukraine around half its expected revenues last month alone.

The Ukrainian prime minister, Serhii Koretskyi, has asked lawmakers to impose austerity measures. Yet there are limits to what can be cut.

“We cannot compromise on supporting our military, because it’s about our survival,” said Oleksandr Merezhko, chairman of the foreign affairs committee in Ukraine’s Parliament. Cutting some of the largest expenses, such as soldiers’ salaries or family payouts, is a nonstarter, he said. “It should be sacred for us.”
How can the gap be filled?

Though Ukraine’s funding shortfall caught much of the E.U. by surprise, Brussels is trying to figure out how to patch it, should that prove necessary.

Valdis Dombrovskis, the E.U. economy commissioner, talked with Mr. Koretskyi on Monday. Step 1 is “to get a clear picture of what the budgetary or financial situation is,” Balazs Ujvari, a spokesman for the European Commission, said following that meeting.

Mr. Zelensky has made suggestions for how Europe could help, such as by speeding up its loan to Ukraine.

The European Union in April finalized that massive loan to Ukraine only after a bruising political process. The lifeline of more than $100 billion is meant to be paid out over two years, half in 2026 and half in 2027.

Paying it out faster may be the only workable option for getting Ukraine more cash quickly, eight European diplomats and officials agreed. Some European officials have suggested that momentum is building behind such a plan.

“We will continue to provide funding through the Ukraine support loan and, where possible, bring that funding forward where it is needed,” Helen McEntee, Ireland’s foreign minister, said following a meeting of defense ministers last week.

That is far from agreed upon, given that officials at the European Commission are only now assessing the size of the funding gap. And it would create another problem: less money for later next year.

Ukraine is also pushing the European Union to seize Russian sovereign assets — a way to rapidly raise an even larger block of funding.

There are more than $200 billion of frozen Russian assets held in the financial depository Euroclear, in Belgium. European officials last year looked at taking that cash and using it to back a loan to Ukraine, but the plan crumbled at the last minute amid opposition from Belgium and other nations.

Now, Sweden and other E.U. nations are trying to bring back the idea of using that money as a way to back Ukraine without draining national budget.

Yet the obstacles that toppled the earlier plan remain. Most importantly, Belgium remains skittish, worried that seizing a foreign nation’s assets could trigger a financial crisis by sending a signal that foreign cash can be seized for political reasons, causing those savers to pull their money out of Euroclear and other European financial institutions. Euroclear declined to comment.

Given such barriers, any agreement to use the frozen money would take months, if one is possible at all.

Andrii Sybiha, Ukraine’s foreign minister, recently urged European countries to move quickly on a decision about the frozen assets and not see them only as leverage for later.

“Negotiations are somewhere in the future,” he said, “while funds are needed now.”

text:
Here is why you are wrong:

A nurse-juror may use ordinary life experience to think about evidence that was actually admitted. She may not become an unsworn expert and “testify” to the other eleven about what toxicology reports mean (SEE VIDEO WHERE SHE TOLD REPORTER SHE EXPLAINED WHAT THE TOXICOLOGY REPORT WAS TO THE LONE HOLDOUT). That second step injects extra-record scientific opinion into deliberations. That is extraneous information, and Massachusetts treats that as misconduct.

 The rules that block it

Jurors must decide facts **solely from evidence admitted in court**, using common sense and life experience—not private professional knowledge offered as proof.

By statute, no juror is “better qualified … solely because of his occupation.” G.L. c. 234A, § 70. The model charge says the same about occupation, education, and experience. A nurse does not get a louder vote because she is a nurse.

A juror may not testify as a witness before the other jurors. Mass. Guide to Evidence § 606(a). Doing the same thing in the jury room—qualifying herself, interpreting lab data, and handing the panel an expert opinion—violates that principle.

After verdict, the court can inquire whether **facts not in evidence** reached the jury. That is the *Fidler* “extraneous matter” rule. Life experience applied to courtroom evidence is allowed. New medical facts, independent calculations, or an expert interpretation that never went through oath, foundation, reliability, or cross-examination are not.

The closest analogue is *Fitzpatrick v. Allen*: jurors used a home medical book in the jury room to resolve a medical issue. New trial. Extra-record medical authority is misconduct. A nurse lecturing on TOXICOLOGY reports is the same problem without the book.

Why the nurse example is misconduct

Toxicology opinions come in only through a qualified expert under § 702: helpfulness, sufficient data, reliable method, reliable application. None of that happens in the jury room. The other side cannot cross-examine her. The judge cannot strike a bad opinion. The parties never confront the “evidence.”

If she tells the others, in substance, “as a nurse I can tell you what these levels mean,” she is supplying untested expert testimony. That is not deliberation. It is a secret trial. In a criminal case, once extraneous information is shown, the Commonwealth must prove beyond a reasonable doubt there was no prejudice. One juror’s specialized lecture on a material issue is often enough to undo the verdict.

Bottom line: thinking like a nurse about admitted exhibits is allowed. Giving the jury her expert testimony is not. That is jury misconduct.

text:
What’s actually going on with Samantha Guthries Mom?

Savannah Guthrie’s mother, Nancy Guthrie (84), has been missing since early February 2026 after disappearing from her home in the Catalina Foothills near Tucson, Arizona. Authorities treat the case as a suspected abduction. https://t.co/LbjarqRw7f 
Nancy was last seen the evening of January 31, 2026, after family dropped her off. She was reported missing the next day when she failed to join a virtual church service. Investigators found blood on the porch and released surveillance footage of a masked person at her front door. The FBI and Pima County Sheriff’s Department have led the investigation. https://t.co/psmenjGZvb 
Ransom notes surfaced shortly after her disappearance. One demanded millions in cryptocurrency. A second note, later reported by outlets including NBC News, indicated she had died and been buried, though investigators have not confirmed her death or recovered remains. Redacted versions of notes were released by authorities in late July. Some notes sent to media were later identified as fake; a California man was sentenced in late August for sending fraudulent ransom demands. https://t.co/7EL3Z60k8q 
Savannah took an extended leave from TODAY, missing the 2026 Winter Olympics coverage, and returned to the anchor desk on April 6. She has given emotional interviews (including with Hoda Kotb), made repeated public and on-air pleas, and posted videos asking anyone with information—or those responsible—to come forward. The family has offered a $1 million reward. She has described the situation as ongoing “agony” and said she cries daily while trying to hold onto joy for her children and viewers. https://t.co/CBRJ1qHSOW 
As of early September 2026 (more than seven months later), Nancy has not been found and no suspect has been publicly identified. Investigators say the case is not cold and they continue working DNA, digital evidence, and tips. Savannah made her first red-carpet appearance since the disappearance in late August at a U.S. Open event with her husband. Local coverage continues to mark the passing days of the search. https://t.co/YzI73CeDQw 
Anyone with information is asked to contact the FBI at 1-800-CALL-FBI. The family continues to ask the public to come forward, even anonymously.

text:
California medical board puts license of psychiatrist Daniel Fast on probation due to overprescribing, patient death

A Palm Springs psychiatrist whose patient later died of an overdose has accepted four years of probation on his medical license rather than fight accusations of overprescribing.

Dr. Daniel E. Fast settled with the Medical Board of California. He did not admit guilt. Regulators alleged gross negligence, excessive prescribing of controlled substances to a patient with a known addiction history, sloppy records, and failure to offer the overdose-reversal drug Narcan.

The board focused on a 33-year-old man Fast treated from 2019 to 2022 for depression and severe bipolar disorder. The patient already had a record of suicide attempts by overdose, alcohol-use disorder, and substance abuse. Fast prescribed the benzodiazepines Klonopin and Xanax while roughly a dozen other clinicians were also writing the same man opioid painkillers. The patient repeatedly called asking for more Xanax, early refills, and help after he started drinking again. Fast continued the benzos anyway, without urine drug tests or a controlled-substance agreement, and knowing the patient also used marijuana and opioids.

The man died Dec. 11, 2022, of acute oxycodone and Xanax intoxication.

A second, older patient received overlapping benzodiazepines and Ambien from Fast and other doctors with no documented coordination or monitoring.

Fast, licensed since 1977, can keep practicing during probation. He must pay nearly $32,000 in investigation costs, complete prescribing courses, log every controlled substance he writes, file quarterly compliance reports, and stop supervising physician assistants and nurse practitioners.

Source: Ani Gasparyan, "Palm Springs psychiatrist prescribed drugs to addict who died," Palm Springs Desert Sun, September 4, 2026.

Discovered vs. Crawled: What it actually means when pages sit in "Discovered/Crawled - currently not indexed," and how to recognize holistic site quality issues over technical bugs.

Key Takeaways for SEOs & Developers:   Patterns over Inventories: Use the report to verify that your intentional changes (like site migrations or page removals) are processing correctly over time.

Should you convert your website into Markdown to help Large Language Models (LLMs) understand your content better?

Is "llms.txt" worth the effort for SEO? In this episode of Search Off the Record, Martin Splitt and John Mueller from the Google Search Relations team dive deep into the history of Markdown, its rise in the AI era, and whether it holds any real weight for search engine discovery.

In this episode, you’ll learn:

The Origins of Markdown: From John Gruber and Aaron Swartz to its status as the "language of GitHub." Markdown vs. HTML: Why the "cleanliness" of Markdown is tempting for developers but potentially risky for site structure. LLMs & Markdown: Do AI crawlers actually prefer Markdown, or are they already experts at parsing HTML?

The "Parallel Version" Trap: Why creating a separate text/Markdown version of your site for AI can lead to the same maintenance nightmares as dynamic rendering. Use Cases that Make Sense: When Markdown is actually superior (like developer documentation) and when it’s totally unnecessary (like your shoe catalog).

Key Takeaways for SEOs & Developers: Crawlers are built for the "messy" web: Google and other engines have decades of experience parsing HTML. Don't sacrifice discovery: Headers, footers, and sidebars in HTML provide critical context for site structure that a raw Markdown file might lack. Maintenance is king: Avoid the complexity of maintaining two versions of the same content.

“…for the most part you can just try things out. One of the nice parts about websites is, often, if you’re using a CMS, you can just edit the page and it’s live, and it’s done. It’s not that you have to do some big, elaborate …work to put it live.”

July 16, 2026

Should you panic when your Search Console indexing report is showing pages that aren't indexed?

Is a 404 error code always a sign of a broken website?

In this episode of Search Off the Record, Martin Splitt and John Mueller from the Google Search Relations team dive deep into the Page Indexing report in Google Search Console. They unpack why treating this report as a static inventory checklist to "fix" things is the wrong response, how to spot massive SEO-ruining hosting or CDN traps, and why a healthy website doesn't actually need a 100% index rate.

In this episode, you’ll learn:   The Indexing Report Shift: Insights from the Search Console team's Hillel on why you should look for trend lines and systemic patterns rather than treating the report as a giant list of errors.

When 404s are Good: Why expected 404 errors are technically correct for deleted content, and how to survive the "boss panic" of numbers that won't go down.

The Domain Property Advantage: How setting up a domain property handles canonical shifts, www vs. non-www tracking, and performance data much cleaner.

The Site Query vs. Search Console: Why the site: query is an artificial tool that might show old domain moves or hreflang swaps for years, making Search Console your only true source of truth.

Hosting & CDN Traps: How aggressive bot protections, hidden interstitials, and "Soft 200" error pages completely destroy your crawl data and lead to malicious canonicalization.

Discovered vs. Crawled: What it actually means when pages sit in "Discovered/Crawled - currently not indexed," and how to recognize holistic site quality issues over technical bugs.

Key Takeaways for SEOs & Developers:   Patterns over Inventories: Use the report to verify that your intentional changes (like site migrations or page removals) are processing correctly over time.

Forget the Ratio: There is no magic metric for indexed vs. non-indexed pages. Even Google’s own developer documentation has a massive chunk of non-indexed content due to intentional choices.

Watch Out for Soft Blocks: Ensure your security layers or CDNs aren't serving "Are you a bot?" challenge screens to Googlebot with a 200 success code.

Computers Fail (And That's Fine): Minor server blips, failed DNS requests, or temporary 500 errors happen. Google's systems are resilient and will just try again later. (Credit: Google)

1. Sensex Falls 555 Points
A front-page report in Deccan Chronicle says Indian benchmark indices fell on Tuesday as rising crude oil prices and heightened tensions in the Middle East weighed on market sentiment, while the rupee weakened against the US dollar. The Sensex dropped 555.23 points to 75,577.58 and the Nifty-50 declined 144.05 points to 23,635.10. Brent crude futures moved in the $96.78-$99.46 a barrel range amid the US-Iran military stand-off.
Why it matters: Broad-based selling signals caution amid rising geopolitical tensions.
Key detail: The benchmark dropped 555.23 points to 75,577.58 as Brent crude hovered near $99.46.

Source: Deccan Chronicle
Next step: Watch crude trajectories before adjusting equity exposure. Tag @RaviRajanPrasad for his market breakdown.

2. Rupee Drops as Crude Nears Hundred
A front-page report in Financial Express says the Indian rupee recorded its sharpest drop in two months against the American dollar on eight September twenty twenty six, closing at ninety four point eight two rupees per dollar. The decline coincided with benchmark equity indices hitting three month lows as crude oil prices neared one hundred dollars a barrel following renewed hostilities in the Middle East. Market participants expect the Reserve Bank of India to intervene lightly to curb volatility, while domestic sectors like financials and banking faced selling pressure despite gains in smaller companies.
Why it matters: Currency weakness directly impacts import-heavy sectors and inflation expectations.
Key detail: The rupee closed at 94.82 against the dollar, marking its sharpest two-month decline.

Source: Financial Express
Next step: Monitor RBI commentary for potential forex intervention. Tag @ChristinaTitusFE for currency analysis.

3. Nifty Swings 850 Points On Expiry
A front-page report in Financial Express says the NSE benchmark index Nifty witnessed extreme volatility on Tuesday, its weekly expiry day, recording a total swing of 850 points and closing at 23,635.10, down 144.05 points. NSE recorded 2,099 crore rupee turnover during the closing auction session, more than double the previous day, with HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Bharti Airtel, and Reliance Industries among the most traded stocks. A similar volatility was recorded in the Sensex on September 3, where the index swung nearly 4,000 points amid weekly expiry, sending option premiums surging by 400 to 500 percent.
Why it matters: Extreme weekly expiry volatility tests derivatives hedging strategies.
Key detail: NSE recorded ₹2,099 crore in the closing auction, with HDFC Bank and Reliance leading volume.

Source: Financial Express
Next step: Review option premium spikes before entering new positions. Tag @VinodNairGeojit for expiry tactics.

A front-page report in Financial Express says domestic markets extended their losing streak amid selling in banking, IT, oil and gas and realty shares, while the BSE Smallcap rose 0.37% to a record closing high of 59,080.20. Vinod Nair, head of research at Geojit Investments, attributed the rally in mid-caps and small-caps to a recovery in domestic inflows and value buying with concerns over earnings downgrade stemming from the 2025 global economic slowdown, elevated inflation and geopolitical uncertainties such as trade tariffs having eased. The BSE Midcap index and BSE Smallcap rose 0.2% each, with pharma and healthcare bucking the trend of sectoral losers.
Why it matters: Sectoral divergence reveals where smart money is rotating.

Next step: Shift focus to mid-cap value plays. Tag @VinodNairGeojit on domestic liquidity trends.

According to Press Monitor's tracking of Indian publications, this media monitoring and print media monitoring review delivers 15 essential stories on social media and digital platforms. This press review covers regulatory actions, corporate moves, and cultural shifts shaping how India engages online. From Australian legislation targeting big tech algorithms to India's own digital engagement strategies, these stories offer critical insights for anyone following news on social media regulation and platform governance.

1. Australia Targets Big Tech Algorithms
A front-page report in Business Standard says Australia has unveiled draft legislation allowing social media users to bypass algorithmic recommendations, deepening global efforts to regulate big tech. Under the Digital Duty of Care bill, platforms such as Meta, TikTok, and Snap must provide non-personalised feed options and face penalties up to one hundred nine point two million Australian dollars for breaches. The proposal follows recent parliamentary moves in France and ongoing investigations by European regulators aiming to curb addictive design features.
Australia's Digital Duty of Care bill requires platforms like Meta, TikTok, and Snap to offer non-personalised feed options, with penalties up to AUD 109.2 million for breaches. This marks a pivotal moment in global efforts to regulate addictive design features and protect users from harmful content.

Why it matters: The legislation sets a precedent that could influence regulatory frameworks worldwide, including in India where similar debates are emerging.

Key detail: Platforms must provide opt-out options for algorithmic recommendations, giving users genuine control over their feeds.

Source: Business Standard, front-page report.

Next step: Watch for how Indian regulators respond to Australia's bold move.

2. Modi Receives Warm Welcome at Vadodara Gen Z Event
A front-page report in First India says Prime Minister Narendra Modi received a warm welcome at a Viksit Bharat event in Vadodara, Gujarat on Tuesday. The event featured online registration through BookMyShow with over 42,000 applicants and included interactions with students and young professionals using social media visual grammar. Modi employed selfie-style Instagram videos and informal youth-oriented communication to engage Gen Z with a political culture shaped by digital platforms like Instagram, recognising their preference for authenticity and direct engagement.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Gen Z outreach at Maharaja Sayajirao University in Vadodara drew over 42,000 online registrations. The event used Instagram-style selfie videos and informal youth communication to engage a generation shaped by social media.

Why it matters: The ramp politics format signals a new era of direct leader-youth engagement through digital platforms.

Key detail: Modi employed visual grammar familiar to young audiences, recognising their preference for authenticity over traditional political rhetoric.

3. EU Warns Of Nihilistic Terror Threat
A front-page report in Morning Standard says authorities across Europe are confronting a rising threat of nihilistic violent extremism fueled by youth seeking status through online communities. Investigators from nine nations recently disrupted thousands of web addresses tied to decentralized digital networks that glorify senseless acts, intensifying counter-terrorism efforts ahead of the twenty-fifth anniversary of the September 11 attacks.
EU Counter-Terrorism Coordinator Bartjan Wegter flagged rising nihilistic violent extremism among online youths, with investigators from nine nations disrupting thousands of web addresses tied to decentralized digital networks.

Why it matters: The threat intensifies ahead of the 25th anniversary of September 11, highlighting how social media fuels radicalisation without political motives.

4. PM Modi Reviews 20 MoS Work

Modi encouraged ministers to share ideas for achieving the vision of a developed India by 2047 and stressed the importance of engaging with young people and using social media platforms effectively.

5. Huda Zariwala Arrested Over Mosque Demolition
A front-page report in Indian Express says police arrested Huda Zariwala on charges of breach of peace after she created a disturbance at Saharanpur’s Circuit House during a visit by Leader of Opposition Lal Bihari Yadav. Authorities lodged an additional First Information Report against her for allegedly sharing objectionable online content following the recent demolition of a local mosque. A court has subsequently remanded her to judicial custody.

6. Trump Map Sparks Diplomatic Outrage
A front-page report in Asian Age says President Donald Trump sparked international fury by posting a digital map colouring Canada, Greenland, Iceland, Mexico and the Caribbean as United States territory. Iceland summoned the United States ambassador to denounce the image as wholly inappropriate amid escalating trade tensions and retaliatory tariffs between Washington and Ottawa. Separately, the Trump administration petitioned the Supreme Court to reinstate a federal immigration database for verifying state voter rolls following a lower court block.
President Donald Trump posted a digital map colouring Canada, Greenland, Iceland, Mexico, and the Caribbean as United States territory on Truth Social, prompting Iceland to summon the US ambassador and sparking international fury.

A front-page report in Tribune says that the Punjab Agri Export Corporation Limited has invited online bids for the engagement of branding, marketing, social media and public relations agency services. 10. FIR Registered Over 'Purification' Ritual After Kharge Event
A front-page report in Hindustan Times says an FIR has been registered against an unidentified person in Haldwani, Uttarakhand, for allegedly conducting a purification ritual at a public ground after a Congress event attended by party president Mallikarjun Kharge last month and for circulating an allegedly doctored video to incite communal and caste-based enmity. The case was lodged at the Haldwani police station on Monday based on a complaint by local advocate and social worker Anju, who alleged the ritual amounted to caste-based discrimination and public humiliation. Police superintendent Manoj Katyal said the FIR names one unidentified individual, with more names to be added if others are identified during the probe.

A front-page report in First India says a 22-year-old student named Rakesh died by suicide at Hotel Garvit in Vaishali Nagar, Jaipur, after posting a social media message that he had failed to live up to his parents' expectations. His cousin, Mangal Chand, became alarmed after receiving no response to repeated calls and arrived at the hotel with acquaintances, where they broke open the locked room and found Rakesh dead with a rope in his bag. The body was sent to Kanwatia Hospital for post-mortem on Monday and handed over to the family while police continue their investigation.

A front-page report in Business Standard says that a new book assessing India's industrial policy highlights how only five percent of the workforce possesses vocational skills, trailing South Korea's ninety-five percent. The analysis points out that manufacturing employment elasticity has steadily declined alongside rising gross domestic product growth since nineteen eighty-three, pushing job creation onto the informal sector. Furthermore, it criticises persistent workplace gender biases and stresses the urgent need to align academic curricula with actual industrial requirements.
Only 5% of India's workforce possesses vocational skills, trailing South Korea's 95%. Manufacturing employment elasticity has declined since 1983, pushing job creation onto the informal sector. Why it matters: The skills gap is a structural barrier to employment growth. Key detail: 5% workforce with vocational skills vs South Korea's 95%. Source: Business Standard, New Delhi. What comes next: Aligning academic curricula with industrial requirements is urgent.

19. Amazon India Seller Base Hits 20 Lakh
A front-page report in Free Press Journal says Amazon India's seller base has reached 20 lakh after the e-commerce platform added more than 3 lakh sellers over the past 12 months, marking its strongest year-on-year expansion in three years. Key drivers included zero referral fees on products priced below ₹1,000 and increased adoption of artificial intelligence tools among selling partners. Ahead of the festive season, Amazon India has created more than 1.6 lakh seasonal employment opportunities across its nationwide operations network spanning 400 cities, including Varanasi, Kochi, Ranchi and Gorakhpur.
Amazon India's seller base reached 20 lakh after adding 3+ lakh sellers over 12 months. The platform created 1.6 lakh seasonal employment opportunities across 400 cities ahead of the festive season. Why it matters: E-commerce is a significant informal job creator. Key detail: 1.6 lakh seasonal jobs across 400 cities. Source: Free Press Journal, Mumbai. What comes next: Festive season hiring will test the sustainability of these opportunities.

As these stories show, print media monitoring reveals the full picture of India's evolving labour market—from AI-driven hiring to rural employment schemes. Which trend will shape your career next?

text:
23 Pivotal Industrials & Manufacturing Stories for CFOs
https://t.co/3RFgdotd7z

Today’s media monitoring report covers news on industrials & manufacturing. This press review distills the day’s most critical developments from leading national publications, giving you actionable insights without the noise. According to Press Monitor's tracking of Indian publications, here are the top stories shaping policy, investment, and production right now.

2. Factory Leasing To Triple By 2030
A front-page report in Economic Times says leasing of factory space by manufacturing companies in India is projected to rise to 30-32 million sq ft annually by 2030 from 21.3 million sq ft in 2025. The report by Savills highlights India's industrial land bank of 4,249 parks spanning 1.6 million acres with over 253,600 acres readily available. Key hubs include Pune, Chennai, and Bengaluru, with government initiatives such as Make in India and PLI driving the transition from Make in India to Made by India.
Why it matters: Industrial real estate demand is accelerating rapidly, signaling strong confidence among manufacturers scaling operations ahead of festive seasons and export pushes.
Key detail: Savills projects leasing to reach 30–32 million sq ft annually by 2030, up from 21.3 million sq ft in 2025, driven by Make in India and PLI schemes across Pune, Chennai, and Bengaluru.

Source: Economic Times
Next step: Evaluate lease terms in emerging hubs and align capex with projected space requirements.

4. Delhi Overhauls Industrial and Startup Policies
A front-page report in Millennium Post says Delhi is moving to overhaul its industrial and startup ecosystem, with the government accelerating work on the proposed Delhi Industrial Policy 2026-2036 and Delhi Startup Policy 2026-2031. Industries Minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa reviewed progress on Tuesday and directed officials to adhere to fixed timelines for single-window clearances, export promotion, and MSME reforms. The proposed industrial policy will focus on clean and sustainable industries, identifying sectors such as frontier technologies, Global Capability Centres, data centres, healthcare, urban logistics, circular economy, green transition, and industry-linked skilling.
Why it matters: State-level policy reforms directly impact compliance timelines, MSME support, and frontier tech adoption.
Key detail: Industries Minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa mandated fixed timelines for single-window clearances, targeting clean industries, data centres, and green transition sectors.

Source: Millennium Post
Next step: Track Delhi’s updated clearance portals and adjust startup incorporation strategies accordingly.

5. Household Manufacturing GVA Surges Faster
A front-page report in Economic Times says household manufacturing gross value added expanded at a compound annual rate of twenty-five point two per cent between financial years twenty-three and twenty-five, significantly outpacing corporate manufacturers at six point seven per cent. This rapid growth underscores the shifting balance toward smaller unincorporated enterprises and improved statistical tracking of informal activities across India. Economists note the trend reflects both genuine enterprise expansion and structural changes in national accounting benchmarks.
Why it matters: Unincorporated enterprises are outpacing corporate manufacturers, reshaping supply chain dynamics and tax reporting benchmarks.
Key detail: Household manufacturing GVA expanded at 25.2% CAGR between FY23 and FY25, compared to 6.7% for corporate peers, reflecting genuine informal sector expansion.

Source: Economic Times
Next step: Adjust vendor onboarding models to capture micro-manufacturer growth.

6. 14 New Industrial Parks Planned
A front-page report in Millennium Post says an industrial roadmap unveiled for the Malwa region includes a land bank of 3,500 hectares, four new industrial parks, and 5,00,000 employment opportunities across 2,781 villages in the regional value chain. The plan designates Pithampur for electric vehicles and advanced engineering, Ujjain as an industrial anchor, Ratlam for logistics and trade, and Indore for start-ups and FinTech.
Why it matters: Regional value chains are being formalized, unlocking massive employment and logistics opportunities outside metro corridors.
Key detail: Malwa region roadmap allocates 3,500 hectares across four parks, designating Pithampur for EVs, Indore for FinTech, and Ratlam for logistics.

Source: Millennium Post
Next step: Map supplier networks to Madhya Pradesh’s new industrial nodes.

7. Rs 2,365 Crore Indore-Pithampur Corridor
A front-page report in Millennium Post says Chief Minister Dr Mohan Yadav laid the foundation stone at Nainod village on May 3 for the first phase of the Indore-Pithampur Economic Corridor. The project is a 100-km Metro Industrial Economic Zone connecting Pithampur through Indore and Ujjain with the Delhi-Mumbai Expressway near Garoth. The first phase comprises a 20-km-long, 75-metre-wide road costing Rs 2,365 crore, with farmers from 17 villages receiving back 60 per cent of their developed land under the land-pooling model.
Why it matters: Mega-infrastructure projects reduce transit times and lower freight costs for heavy manufacturing.
Key detail: Chief Minister Dr Mohan Yadav inaugurated the first phase of a 20-km, 75-metre-wide road connecting Pithampur through Indore and Ujjain to the Delhi-Mumbai Expressway.

Source: Millennium Post
Next step: Reassess distribution center locations along the new economic zone.

8. 51.9 Percent Rise In Electric Vehicle Retail
A front-page report in Business Standard says that electric vehicle penetration continued to rise in August despite a sequential moderation in registrations ahead of the festive season. Electric passenger vehicle retail rose 51.9 per cent year-on-year to 30,696 units, while electric two-wheelers grew 67.1 per cent to 183,204 units. Tata Motors retained a commanding lead in electric passenger vehicles, with VinFast climbing to fourth place with 2,199 units.
Why it matters: EV adoption is accelerating despite seasonal moderation, impacting auto component suppliers and battery logistics.
Key detail: Passenger EV retail hit 30,696 units (+51.9% YoY), while two-wheelers surged 67.1% to 183,204 units, with VinFast climbing to fourth place.

Source: Business Standard
Next step: Review inventory turnover rates for legacy ICE components.

9. RIICO E-Auction Nets 376 Crore Rupees
A front-page report in First India says strong investor appetite for Rajasthan industrial land was evident in RIICO's recent e-auction of land parcels, which attracted more than 200 online applications for 102 plots. Bidding was successfully completed for plots spread across nearly 62 acres across industrial areas including Ajmer, Alwar, Bhiwadi, Ghiloth, Jaipur, Nagaur, Pali, Kota, and Sawai Madhopur, with a combined value of around Rs 376 crore.
Why it matters: Rajasthan’s land allocation strategy is attracting serious capital inflows for manufacturing clusters.
Key detail: Over 200 online applications competed for 102 plots across Ajmer, Alwar, Bhiwadi, Jaipur, and Kota, securing Rs 376 crore in committed investments.

Source: First India
Next step: Monitor upcoming RIICO tender rounds for strategic site selection.

10. Output PPI Inflation Could Aid Deflator Fall
A front-page report in Business Standard says the use of double deflators for the manufacturing sector in the recently released gross domestic product data has sparked a controversy. Input producer price index for manufactured goods is at a trial stage, so output producer price index for items used in the manufacturing segment was used and subtracted from the output producer price index for manufactured products to arrive at deflators for the segment. Assuming that producer price index inflation for April also behaved similarly, output producer price index inflation for factory inputs in aggregate must have risen over eleven per cent in the first quarter to produce a fall in deflators.
Why it matters: Shifting GDP calculation methodologies may alter how manufacturers report margin pressures and input costs.
Key detail: Double deflator usage suggests factory input PPI inflation exceeded 11% in Q1, potentially compressing reported sectoral margins.

Source: Business Standard
Next step: Stress-test pricing models against revised deflator baselines.

11. Yogi Adityanath Champions UP Textile Growth
A front-page report in The Hans India says Minister Yogi Adityanath asserted on Tuesday that Uttar Pradesh has transformed significantly since two thousand seventeen, shifting from periods of unrest and policy paralysis to an era defined by the rule of law, investor confidence, and rapid industrial expansion. Speaking at the inaugural session of the two-day Uttar Pradesh Textile Conclave two zero two six, he emphasised the state government’s commitment to building an integrated ecosystem across the entire textile value chain, positioning the state as a region of unlimited potential.
Why it matters: Uttar Pradesh is positioning itself as a complete textile ecosystem hub, influencing raw material sourcing and labor policies.
Key detail: The state government pledged integrated value-chain support at the UP Textile Conclave 2026, emphasizing investor confidence and rapid industrial expansion.

Source: The Hans India
Next step: Engage with UP textile cluster associations for subsidy alignment.

12. GMDC Copper Project Ambaji Recruitment
A front-page report in Times of India says Gujarat Mineral Development Corporation Ltd invites experienced professionals for key leadership roles at the Copper Project in Ambaji, Gujarat. Open positions include General Manager of Mines and General Manager of Plant to lead underground mining operations and beneficiation plant development. Applicants can find more information at the company website.
Why it matters: Critical mineral extraction projects are scaling leadership teams, creating high-value engineering roles.
Key detail: Gujarat Mineral Development Corporation is hiring General Managers for Mines and Plant operations to accelerate underground mining and beneficiation.

Source: Times of India
Next step: Align talent acquisition pipelines with Gujarat’s mining expansion timeline.

13. 53% EV Growth Sets August Record
A front-page report in Deccan Herald says HCLTech has launched an advanced Semiconductor Lab in Bengaluru with an investment of Rs 185 crore. The 40,000 sq ft facility features cleanrooms and delivers end-to-end post-silicon engineering, advanced testing, and failure analysis for global customers.
Why it matters: Record monthly sales validate sustained consumer demand and fleet electrification momentum.
Key detail: August EV sales surpassed 2.98 lakh units (+53% YoY), with electric commercial vehicles tripling to 4,702 units, marking FADA’s best month ever.

Source: Business Line
Next step: Update fleet replacement forecasts for commercial transport partners.

14. Over 11% PPI Factory Input Inflation
A front-page report in Business Standard says over 11 percent PPI factory input inflation could have contributed to a fall in GDP deflators for the manufacturing sector. The methodology of using double deflators in the recently released GDP data has sparked controversy due to the opaque nature of computing these deflators. Input producer price index for manufactured goods remains at a trial stage, complicating the calculations.
Why it matters: Persistent input cost pressures require proactive hedging and contract renegotiation strategies.
Key detail: Opaque double-deflator calculations highlight rising factory input prices, complicating margin visibility for mid-tier manufacturers.

Source: Business Standard
Next step: Lock in long-term supplier agreements before Q3 price revisions.

15. Rs 2,365 Crore UIMR Road Project
A front-page report in Millennium Post says the Ujjain-Indore Metropolitan Region has been notified as a single planning unit spanning 16,000.87 sq km across six districts, with plans for five lakh new employment opportunities. Chief Minister Dr Mohan Yadav laid the foundation stone for the Indore-Pithampur Economic Corridor first phase at Nainod village on May 3, comprising a 20-km road costing Rs 2,365 crore. The framework, aligned with Viksit Bharat 2047, envisions shared infrastructure, integrated planning, and seven regional growth nodes to ensure balanced development beyond Indore and Ujjain.
Why it matters: Metropolitan regional planning is integrating infrastructure, employment, and sustainable development frameworks.
Key detail: The Ujjain-Indore Metropolitan Region notification covers 16,000 sq km across six districts, targeting five lakh jobs through seven growth nodes aligned with Viksit Bharat 2047.

Source: Millennium Post
Next step: Participate in regional planning consultations for land-use zoning.

16. Coal Gasification Scheme Targets Import Substitution
A front-page report in Financial Express says the Indian government has launched a scheme to convert domestic coal and lignite into higher-value products like syngas, methanol, ammonia, urea, and hydrogen to reduce fuel and raw material imports. The initiative builds on an earlier 8,500-crore rupee incentive programme approved in January 2024, with financial incentives of up to 20 percent of eligible plant and machinery costs now available. Industry leaders including Dasur Energy CEO Atanu Mukherjee note that major companies such as Adani and NTPC are treating coal gasification as a serious industrial investment proposition.
Why it matters: Domestic fuel conversion initiatives are reducing reliance on imported LNG and industrial feedstocks.
Key detail: The Centre offers up to 20% financial incentives on plant costs, with Adani and NTPC treating coal-to-syngas projects as core strategic investments.

Source: Financial Express
Next step: Assess eligibility for gasification subsidies if operating in chemical or fertilizer segments.

17. Rs 3 Lakh Crore Coal Gasification
A front-page report in Financial Express says India received seven proposals for the coal gasification scheme under which domestic coal and lignite would be converted into syngas, methanol, ammonia, urea and hydrogen. The first application window closed on September seventy, with Round 2 opening on September eight. Atanu Mukherjee, chief executive officer of Dasar Energy, noted that the financial incentive framework can help absorb early-stage risk but projects must demonstrate sustainable returns.
Why it matters: Massive capital deployment signals a structural shift toward energy independence and circular industrial economies.
Key detail: Seven proposals closed the first window, with Round 2 opening September 8; Dasur Energy CEO Atanu Mukherjee notes early-stage risk absorption is critical.

Source: Financial Express
Next step: Prepare feasibility studies for co-processing facilities near lignite belts.

18. GE Vernova T&D India Gains 8.9% On Order Boost
A front-page report in Business Standard says GE Vernova T&D India secured L1 status for the Barmer II-South Kalamb HVDC order from Power Grid, estimated at Rs 13,000 crore. Revenue recognition is likely to start around FY29, boosting order inflows to Rs 23,100 crore.
Why it matters: Grid modernization contracts are driving immediate revenue recognition cycles for power equipment manufacturers.
Key detail: GE Vernova secured L1 status for Barmer II-South Kalamb HVDC from Power Grid (~Rs 13,000 crore), with revenue ramp-up expected by FY29.

Source: Business Standard
Next step: Coordinate procurement schedules with grid expansion milestones.

19. HCLTech Launches Rs 185 Crore Semiconductor Lab
A front-page report in Deccan Herald says HCLTech has launched an advanced Semiconductor Lab in Bengaluru with an investment of Rs 185 crore. The 40,000 sq ft facility features cleanrooms and delivers end-to-end post-silicon engineering, advanced testing, and failure analysis for global customers.
Why it matters: Advanced testing and failure analysis capabilities are strengthening India’s position in global chip supply chains.
Key detail: The 40,000 sq ft Bengaluru facility delivers end-to-end post-silicon engineering for international semiconductor clients.

Source: Deccan Herald
Next step: Explore partnership pathways for validation services and R&D collaboration.

20. Seven Proposals For Coal Gasification Scheme
A front-page report in Financial Express says the Centre's Rs 37,500 crore coal gasification incentive scheme has drawn seven proposals from five companies in its first round, with Adani Enterprises submitting three urea projects and NTPC proposing a synthetic natural gas facility. The government aims to develop 75 million tonnes of coal and lignite gasification capacity under the scheme to reduce India's import bill for LNG and key industrial feedstocks.
Why it matters: Early industry uptake demonstrates strong appetite for import-substitution technologies amid volatile commodity markets.
Key detail: Adani Enterprises submitted three urea projects and NTPC proposed synthetic natural gas, supporting the government’s 75 MMT capacity target.

Source: Financial Express
Next step: Monitor regulatory approvals for feedstock allocation and environmental clearances.

21. Balmer Lawrie 160th Year Recruitment
A front-page report in Times of India says Balmer Lawrie and Company Limited, a Government of India Enterprise, has opened multiple recruitment posts across India including Assistant Manager, Deputy Manager, Officer, and Junior Officer roles. The vacancies span locations such as Kolkata, Mumbai, Chennai, Vadodara, Bengaluru, Delhi, Hyderabad, and Cochin, with a submission deadline of 29 September 2026. The company marks 160 years of trust, reliability, and transparency with presence in industrial packaging, greases, lubricants, chemicals, logistics, and travel.
Why it matters: Legacy government enterprises are expanding operational footprints across logistics, chemicals, and industrial packaging.
Key detail: Multiple managerial and officer vacancies span Kolkata, Mumbai, Chennai, Vadodara, Bengaluru, Delhi, Hyderabad, and Cochin, closing September 29.

Source: Times of India
Next step: Submit applications for leadership tracks aligned with public-sector manufacturing goals.

22. Industrial Parks Adopt Zero Liquid Discharge
A front-page report in Millennium Post says industrial parks are proposed to use Zero Liquid Discharge systems so untreated industrial wastewater is not released into natural water sources. The plan includes large-scale solar and wind projects in Agar-Malwa and surrounding districts with the objective of developing carbon-neutral industrial clusters. Restrictions on construction near the Narmada, other water bodies, and forests are also incorporated along with plantation programmes.
Why it matters: Environmental compliance standards are becoming mandatory for industrial cluster financing and ESG ratings.
Key detail: Agar-Malwa parks will implement ZLD systems alongside large-scale solar/wind projects to achieve carbon-neutral manufacturing zones.

Source: Millennium Post
Next step: Integrate water recycling audits into facility upgrade budgets.

23. Rs 91.61 Crore Gwalior Telecom Manufacturing Tender
A front-page report in Hindustan Times says Madhya Pradesh Industrial Development Corporation Ltd has invited online engineering procurement construction bids for infrastructure work at a telecommunications manufacturing zone in Gwalior. The project carries a probable contract value of Rs 91.61 crore and is targeted at registered contractors and firms operating across the district.
Why it matters: Public procurement pipelines are actively funding telecom hardware assembly and electronics manufacturing zones.
Key detail: MPIDC invited EPC bids for infrastructure work at Gwalior’s telecom manufacturing park, targeting registered contractors and engineering firms.

Source: Hindustan Times
Next step: Register on state procurement portals and bid for civil works packages.

24. Tender Notices For 2026 Brahmotsavam And Power Projects
A front-page report in The Hindu says e-tenders have been invited by the Sri Venkateswara Bhakti Channel in Tirupati for camera setups and Jimmy Jibs for the Srivari Salakatla Brahmotsavam 2026. MSETCL invites bids for a 220/33kV substation in Maharashtra, while BESCOM seeks quotations for annual maintenance contracts on cable fault locators in Karnataka.
Why it matters: Diverse infrastructure spending spans cultural events, power transmission, and distribution maintenance across multiple states.
Key detail: MSETCL seeks bids for a 220/33kV substation in Maharashtra, while BESCOM requests annual maintenance contracts for cable fault locators in Karnataka.

Source: The Hindu
Next step: Align bidding teams with regional utility tender calendars.

25. 5.06 Percent Skills Shortfall Hampers Indian Industry
A front-page report in Business Standard says that a new book assessing India's industrial policy highlights how only five percent of the workforce possesses vocational skills, trailing South Korea's ninety-five percent. The analysis points out that manufacturing employment elasticity has steadily declined alongside rising gross domestic product growth since nineteen eighty-three, pushing job creation onto the informal sector. Furthermore, it criticises persistent workplace gender biases and stresses the urgent need to align academic curricula with actual industrial requirements.
Why it matters: Workforce capability gaps remain a critical bottleneck for scaling advanced manufacturing and automation.
Key detail: Only 5% of India’s workforce holds vocational skills versus South Korea’s 95%, with declining manufacturing employment elasticity pushing job creation into the informal sector.

Source: Business Standard
Next step: Partner with technical institutes to co-design curriculum modules for next-gen machinery.

text:
13 Essential Human Resources Stories for HR Leaders
https://t.co/pp561bQ29V

According to Press Monitor's tracking of Indian publications, this news on human resources and media monitoring and print media monitoring report covers 13 defining stories spanning hiring surges, labor actions, and workforce policy shifts across India.

1. Eiffel Tower Reopens After Gender Strike
A front-page report in Hindustan Times says the Eiffel Tower reopened on Tuesday after a one-day staff strike protested management instructions limiting female workers' contact with a visiting Hindu delegation. The landmark operators admitted the conditions were unacceptable, prompting Paris mayor Emmanuel Gregoire to launch two official investigations into the gender-based discrimination claim. The religious group behind the visit issued an apology and stated the request was never intended as gender-rooted.
The Eiffel Tower reopened after a one-day staff strike over gender-based restrictions during a Hindu delegation's visit. Paris Mayor Emmanuel Gregoire launched two investigations, and the landmark operators admitted the conditions were unacceptable. Why it matters: workplace discrimination claims now reach global iconic institutions, forcing operators to review visitor protocols. Key detail: two formal investigations ordered. Source: Hindustan Times. What will the Eiffel Tower's operating company change about visitor management policies?

2. Government Workers Extend Strike in Chandigarh and Mohali
A front-page report in Tribune says employees in Chandigarh and Mohali have extended their protest until Friday, demanding the government withdraw orders declaring mass casual leave as unauthorised. Union leaders refused to call off the agitation after talks with Principal Secretary KK Yadav, while the government directed administrative secretaries to impose no work no pay penalties on striking workers. The movement centres on long-pending demands including dearness allowance arrears and restoration of the Old Pension Scheme.
Punjab government employees extended their pen-down strike until Friday, demanding dearness allowance arrears and restoration of the Old Pension Scheme. The government invoked no-work no-pay penalties after talks failed. Why it matters: public sector labor unrest is escalating across states, threatening essential services. Key detail: strike extended to Friday. Source: Tribune. Will the Punjab government concede to the workers' demands before Friday?

3. Assam Teacher Law Faces Court Challenge
A front-page report in Statesman says petitioners challenge the two thousand seventeen Assam law permitting teacher provincialisation without prescribed qualifications, citing potential violations of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, the National Council for Teacher Education Act one nine hundred ninety three, and the University Grants Commission Act one nine five six. The public interest litigation seeks to restrain further government teaching appointments through this procedure and demands transparent, merit-based recruitment aligned with constitutional guarantees and statutory eligibility norms. Counseled by senior advocates Ranjit Kumar and Chandra Bhushan Prasad, the matter awaits further judicial review on September twenty second.
The Supreme Court is hearing a public interest litigation challenging the 2017 Assam law permitting teacher provincialisation without prescribed qualifications. Petitioners cite violations of the Right to Education Act and NCTE Act. Why it matters: the ruling could set a precedent for teacher recruitment standards nationwide. Key detail: court notice issued to Centre and state government. Source: Statesman. How will this ruling affect teacher appointments across India?

4. Govt Pauses PLI Scheme Amid Strike Threat
A front-page report in Business Line says the government has temporarily put on hold the implementation of the new Performance Linked Incentive scheme for financial year 2025-26 following a meeting between Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman and bank employees. The Union Finance Ministry stated the PLI scheme will now be discussed during ongoing bipartite settlement and joint note discussions, with the issue to be renegotiated mutually between bank unions and management through official bilateral discussions. The United Forum of Bank Unions has announced a series of strikes beginning with a one-day strike on September 11 over unresolved key demands including a five-day banking week and the government's revised PLI scheme.
The government temporarily halted the Performance Linked Incentive scheme for public sector banks after Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman met bank employee representatives. The United Forum of Bank Unions announced a one-day strike on September 11. Why it matters: bank employee welfare and incentive structures are under national scrutiny. Key detail: PLI scheme to be renegotiated bilaterally. Source: Business Line. What concessions will bank unions seek in the upcoming bipartite talks?

5. Rs 30,000 Stipend Demand Ends Strike
A front-page report in Indian Express says medical interns in Srinagar called off their strike after meeting Health Minister Sakina Itoo, with the stipend matter to be finalized within 30 days. The Madhya Pradesh Police has ordered an inquiry into the use of a water cannon on protesting intern doctors at Hamidia Hospital in Bhopal, where some protesters were reportedly injured.
Medical interns in Srinagar called off their strike after Health Minister Sakina Itoo pledged to resolve the stipend increase from Rs 12,300 to Rs 30,000 within 30 days. Meanwhile, Madhya Pradesh Police ordered an inquiry into a water cannon incident at Hamidia Hospital in Bhopal. Why it matters: intern welfare and healthcare workforce conditions remain critical national issues. Key detail: stipend matter to be finalized within 30 days. Source: Indian Express. Will the Madhya Pradesh inquiry lead to policy changes for healthcare workers?

6. PM SHRI School Leh Walk-in Interview
A front-page report in Tribune says a walk-in interview for contract posts at PM Shri Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya in Leh, Ladakh, is scheduled for 11 September 2026. The vacancies are for TGT (Hindi) and Counsellor (Male), with essential qualifications including a four-year integrated degree from an NCERT or NCTE recognised institution, a Bachelors Honours Degree, or a Bachelor's Degree, plus CTET and B.Ed for the teaching post, and a Masters Degree in Psychology plus a one-year Diploma in Guidance and Counselling for the counsellor post. Honorarium is Rs 40,625 for TGT (Hindi) and Rs 44,900 for Counsellor (Male), and candidates must bring original documents and attested copies.
A walk-in interview for contract posts at PM Shri Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya in Leh, Ladakh, is scheduled for September 11, 2026, with vacancies for TGT Hindi and Counsellor Male. Why it matters: remote region education recruitment highlights the government's commitment to staffing underserved schools. Key detail: honorarium of Rs 40,625 for TGT and Rs 44,900 for Counsellor. Source: Tribune. Are enough qualified candidates expected to apply for these Ladakh positions?

7. 9% Hiring Growth Across India
A front-page report in The Hans India says hiring growth was broad-based across IT and non-IT sectors, with auto industry up 19 percent, healthcare 16 percent, and retail 15 percent. Hiring rose 10 percent for 4-7 year experience and 6 percent for those with 8-12 years, while freshers grew 15 percent. Hyderabad led metros with 23 percent growth, followed by Kolkata 22 percent and Chennai 20 percent.
Hiring growth rose 9 percent year-on-year across IT and non-IT sectors, with auto up 19 percent, healthcare 16 percent, and retail 15 percent. Hyderabad led metros with 23 percent growth. Why it matters: broad-based hiring signals economic recovery across diverse sectors. Key detail: freshers hiring grew 15 percent. Source: The Hans India. Which sector will lead hiring momentum in the coming quarter?

8. Samsung India Lays Off Dozens Of Staff
A front-page report in The Hans India says Samsung India has laid off eight to ten mid-to-senior level employees and plans to dismiss another forty to fifty workers in its consumer electronics division over the coming weeks. The workforce reduction aims to improve efficiency and manage rising input costs amid stiff competition from domestic and international rivals. The company is also consolidating regional branch offices across the country.
Samsung India laid off eight to ten mid-to-senior level employees and plans to dismiss another forty to fifty workers in its consumer electronics division. The company is consolidating regional branch offices. Why it matters: global tech firms are restructuring Indian operations amid rising input costs and competition. Key detail: 40-50 additional workers planned for dismissal. Source: The Hans India. How will Samsung's restructuring affect India's consumer electronics job market?

9. White-collar Hiring Up 14%
A front-page report in Business Standard says that India’s white-coloured hiring surged fourteen percent year-on-year in August, led by demand from non-information-technology sectors and stronger freshers hiring, according to the latest Naukri JobSpeak Index report. The index rose to 3,128 from 2,664 a year earlier, though it fell six percent from 3,227 in July, indicating a month-on-month moderation.
India's white-collar hiring surged 14 percent year-on-year in August, led by non-IT sector demand and stronger freshers hiring, per the Naukri JobSpeak Index. The index rose to 3,128 from 2,664 a year earlier. Why it matters: non-IT sectors are driving employment growth, signaling diversification in India's job market. Key detail: index fell 6 percent from July, showing month-on-month moderation. Source: Business Standard. Is the white-collar hiring boom sustainable beyond August?

10. Trade Union Congress Rejects Penny Levy Scheme
A front-page report in Statesman says that Mr. Ben Turner moved an emergency resolution at the Trade Union Congress in Bournemouth, citing concerns over government interference and the unwarranted use of emergency powers in industrial disputes. The resolution passed by an overwhelming majority, affirming the peaceful nature of recent mining negotiations. Conversely, a proposal to collect a penny monthly levy per member to finance the Easton Lodge labour education scheme was rejected after members debated the necessity of reviewing union finances versus funding higher education.
The Trade Union Congress in Bournemouth rejected a penny monthly levy per member to finance the Easton Lodge labour education scheme, while affirming the peaceful nature of recent mining negotiations. Why it matters: union financial decisions impact labor education funding and organizational strategy. Key detail: emergency resolution passed citing government interference concerns. Source: Statesman/Reuters. How will this rejection affect future union education schemes?

11. 30 Sanitation Workers Dismissed In Haryana
A front-page report in Tribune says the Haryana government dismissed 30 contractual sanitation workers and suspended eight regular employees as the sanitation workers' strike entered its 34th day. text:
You got rejected after the final round. Most people close the tab and move on. That's the expensive mistake.

Look at what the company just did. They spent four hours on you. Several people formed an opinion. They now have a file on someone they know is competent and available. That file doesn't expire when the role gets filled — and roles reopen constantly. Someone leaves in month two. Headcount unfreezes. The candidate they picked turns the offer down.

Send this within 24 hours, while you're still a name they recognise:

"Thanks for the time — I'd genuinely appreciate one thing I could work on. And if a similar role opens in the next few months, I'd like to be considered."

Two things make it work. It's short, so answering costs them nothing. And it asks for feedback instead of arguing with the decision — arguing is why most follow-ups get ignored.

Then do the unglamorous part. Write down whatever they tell you. Set a reminder three months out to check their careers page.

A rejection means "not this role, not this week." Most candidates read it as "no" and delete a warm contact at a company that already knows they can do the work.

text:
Compensation benchmarking is one of the biggest challenges in crypto people ops here’s a short brain dump  on how we’ve implemented global comp frameworks at some of the leading projects in crypto that where we have been founding recruiters or trusted embedded partners at @TechChainTalent 

1. Decide on your comp philosophy: are you market lagging, matching or leading. You can be market lagging believe it or not if you provide security, vision, comprehensive benefits, competitive token or equity allocation. 

2. Design a thoroughly thought out levelling framework, include as few people as possible in the beginning, this is where too many cooks can certainly spoil the broth. Anything subjective is hard to codify and you don’t want to over engineer here and there no issue revising and evolving your levelling framework as you mature.

3. Benchmark against the right comparator set. Generic tech salary data will mislead you. Your comparators are the 20 to 40 protocols actually competing for the same engineer, and that list changes depending on whether you are hiring a Rust protocol engineer, a solidity dev, a DevRel or a Head of Growth. Build your own dataset from real offers and live negotiations, not survey averages that are 18 months stale. Also we’re seeing more and more revenue generating focussed roles in crypto, if you don’t have an OTE or bonus component for your sales team you’re going to lose people or worse hire the wrong people. 

4. Split cash and token into two separate conversations. The single biggest mistake we see is quoting one blended number. Cash should stand on its own as a defensible base. Token is upside. When you blend them at an internal valuation nobody outside the company believes, you set expectations you cannot meet at the next review cycle. We’ve been around long enough to know that crypto is volatile, you can counteract that with an annual token grant with a performance based review after 12 months that may even qualify your best talent for a multiplier. 

5.Get your token mechanics right before you make a single offer. Vesting length, cliff, whether allocation is a fixed percentage of supply or a USD value at grant, what happens pre TGE, what happens on a bad leaver. Decide once, write it down, apply it consistently. Changing this in month nine because one candidate pushed back will poison the whole framework.

6. Choose location based or global bands and commit. Global bands are simpler, easier to defend and win you talent in high cost markets. Location bands protect burn and let you hire deep in LATAM, Eastern Europe and SEA. Both work. What does not work is doing global bands quietly for the people who negotiated hardest.

7. Solve payment rails early. Stablecoin payroll, EOR, contractor agreements, local entities. This is not a finance afterthought, it is a hiring constraint. We have lost candidates over a two week delay in figuring out how to pay someone in Argentina.

8.Set a review cadence and stick to it. Twice yearly for cash, annual refresh grants for token. Publish the dates. Most comp anxiety in crypto orgs is not about the number, it is about not knowing when the number gets revisited.

9. Decide your transparency level deliberately. Full public bands, internal transparency, or nothing. Any of the three is fine. What kills trust is partial transparency where people compare notes and find the framework was never applied evenly.

The frameworks that hold up are the boring ones that survive contact with a hot candidate who wants 40 percent above band. If you cannot say no to that person, you do not have a framework, you have a spreadsheet.

Why it matters: The Competition Commission's closure of its Google case marks a pivotal shift in how real money games are regulated in India.
Key detail: The case, filed by Winzo Games in 2022, was investigated under the Online Gaming Act, with Google committing to modify its practices before the new framework took full effect.

Since the box is a model, its design is based on the detailed instructions found in the biblical Book of Exodus .

📖 The "How-To" Guide for a Sacred Object
The instructions for building the Ark were given to Moses on Mount Sinai. It wasn't a massive chest but a relatively portable box built from acacia wood and overlaid with pure gold, inside and out .

Dimensions: It was about 45 inches long, 27 inches wide, and 27 inches high .

Carrying it: It had four gold rings, one on each corner, for poles to be passed through so it could be carried by the Levites without being touched .

✨ More Than Just a Box: What it Held and Meant
The Ark's true significance lay not in its construction, but in its contents and its role as a symbol of God's presence.

What was inside: According to the Bible, it held the most important items from Israel's journey:
The Two Stone Tablets: The primary purpose of the Ark was to house the tablets of the Ten Commandments, often referred to as the "Testimony" .
Aaron's Rod: The staff of Aaron, which miraculously budded to confirm his chosen priesthood .
A Pot of Manna: A jar containing the manna God provided to the Israelites in the desert for food .

The "Mercy Seat": The gold lid of the Ark was called the "Mercy Seat" (or "atonement cover"). The Hebrew word for it is kapporeth, which relates to atonement or propitiation . On top of this seat were two golden cherubim facing each other with their wings spread over the Ark .
God's Throne: The Mercy Seat was considered the footstool or throne of God. It was the place on earth where his divine presence was most powerfully manifested. The Bible says God would meet with Moses and speak to him "from above the mercy seat, from between the two cherubim" .
The Day of Atonement: Once a year, on the Day of Atonement, the High Priest would enter the Holy of Holies and sprinkle the blood of a sacrifice on the Mercy Seat to atone for the sins of the entire nation . The idea was that the blood would cover the sins of the people, satisfying God's justice and allowing for mercy to be shown .
🗺️ A History of Triumph, Tragedy, and Mystery
The Ark wasn't just a passive relic; it was a powerful symbol that played a central and dramatic role in Israel's history.
Entering the Promised Land: When the Israelites first crossed the Jordan River into the Promised Land, the priests carrying the Ark led the way, and the river miraculously parted for them .

The Fall of Jericho: At the siege of Jericho, the Israelites marched around the city for seven days with the Ark leading the procession, culminating in the city's walls collapsing .

Captured and Returned: In a dark period, the Ark was captured by the Philistines in battle. However, it brought misfortune upon them, and they were forced to return it to Israelite territory .

David's Journey: King David famously brought the Ark to Jerusalem with a massive celebration. On this journey, a man named Uzzah touched the Ark to steady it and was struck dead, showing the extreme holiness of the object .
Solomon's Temple: David's son, Solomon, eventually built the great Temple in Jerusalem and placed the Ark in the innermost and holiest chamber, the "Holy of Holies" .

❓ What Happened Next? The Mystery of the Lost Ark

The Ark's fate after the destruction of the First Temple by the Babylonians around 586 BC is a complete mystery. The Bible doesn't say what happened to it .

Theories: Over the centuries, many theories have emerged. Some believe it was hidden in a cave near Jerusalem or beneath the Temple Mount itself. A famous legend claims it is in the Church of Our Lady Mary of Zion in Aksum, Ethiopia .

No Confirmation: Today, its location remains unknown. No definitive archaeological evidence has ever been found, and its disappearance is one of history's great unsolved mysteries.

What's in the box is therefore a miniature replica of a lost object that, for believers, was the ultimate symbol of God's presence, a physical embodiment of his covenant with his people, and the location where divine justice and mercy met.

WHO DID IT KILL
Found 12 web pages

The Ark of the Covenant was directly and indirectly associated with several deaths in the biblical narrative. The most famous direct case is a man named Uzzah.

⚡ The Direct Strike: Uzzah

As King David was transporting the Ark to Jerusalem, the oxen pulling the cart stumbled. Uzzah reached out his hand to steady the Ark, and the Bible says God's anger burned against him for his irreverence, striking him dead on the spot. He died "there beside the ark of God". This was because the Ark was considered so holy that it was never to be touched, and was supposed to be carried by poles on the shoulders of Levites, not on a cart.

⚔️ The Indirect Cost: The Battle Against the Philistines
In a different event, the Israelites brought the Ark into battle against the Philistines, hoping it would secure their victory. Instead, the battle went disastrously:
Israel's Army: The Bible recounts a "very great slaughter" where Israel lost about 30,000 foot soldiers.

Eli's Sons: Among the dead were Hophni and Phinehas, the two sons of the high priest Eli, who had accompanied the Ark.
The Philistines captured the Ark in this battle, though they later returned it due to a series of misfortunes they attributed to it.

So what do you propose, @cabsav456?

1. On the matter of legality of settlements in Area C- correct me if I am wrong but you seem to be arguing that they are illegal under international law. You've repeatedly cited the UN and ICJ line that the violation is of Article 49 of the Fourth Geneva Convention. That assumes that the Fourth Geneva Convention applies de jure to the West Bank. It DOES NOT as  that the territory WAS NOT UNDER THE RECOGNIZED SOVEREIGNTY OF ANY STATE PRIOR TO 1967  Israel contends that settlements do not involve forcible "transfer" by the government in a way that breaches the convention MOREOVER the building is not a violation because it occurs on public and/or LAWFULLY acquired land. 

2.Additionally, fealty to and fandom for the international law  you cite, presumably, would also apply to the requirements for statehood as stipulated under INTERNATIONAL LAW for nearly 100 year. This establishes, under the Montevideo convention,   the following 4 criteria for statehood:

●Permanent population: A group of people living there permanently, though size does not matter.

●Defined territory: A specific land area, even if borders are disputed.

●Government: A political body that exercises effective control over the people and land.

●Capacity to enter relations: The ability to deal with other sovereign nations.
 
Are you asserting that either Gaza or the WB or some amalgamation of both, equaling 'Palestine' meets these requirements? 

Im not sure how, with a straight face you can make that argument  but Im willing to hear you try. 

If, however, you agree these conditions have NOT been met then, respectfully, your entire argument comes crashing down the moment I tug on any one of the flimsy threads youve provided.

3. If ongoing settlement is NOT illegal by virtue of what Ive stated above- you still raise the matter of whether or not settlements are ethical or strategically beneficial. I would state that what is unethical is a Judenrein Area C. As far as strategically beneficial- to whom do you think they should be of strategic benefit? 

4. You raise the issue of Palestinians living indefinitely without citizenship in a territory Israel controls.  That there is no state and therefore no citizenship, is not the fault of Israel but decades of Palestinian rejectionism as follows:

●1937 Peel Commission**: British proposal to partition Mandatory Palestine into a small Jewish state and a larger Arab state (linked to Transjordan), with population transfers. The Arab Higher Committee, led by Haj Amin al-Husseini (photo below), rejected it and demanded a single Arab state.

●1947 UN Partition: Proposed a Jewish state and an Arab state with Jerusalem under international administration. The Jewish Agency accepted it as a basis for a state. The Arab Higher Committee and surrounding Arab states rejected it and launched war after Israel’s declaration of independence in 1948.

●1967 Khartoum Resolution: After the Six-Day War, the Arab League (with Palestinian representation aligned) declared no peace with Israel, no recognition of Israel, and no negotiations with Israel.

●PLO founding documents and early strategy: The original Palestine National Charter called for the elimination of Israel. 

●Hamas 1988 Covenant**: Explicitly rejected Israel’s right to exist, framed the conflict in religious terms, and treated armed struggle as obligatory. 

●Camp David, 2000: Prime Minister Ehud Barak, with U.S. mediation by President Clinton, offered a Palestinian state on most of the West Bank plus Gaza, land swaps, and shared arrangements in Jerusalem. Arafat rejected the package &kicked off the 2nd Second Intifada.

●Olmert offer, 2008: After dozens of meetings, Prime Minister Ehud Olmert presented Mahmoud Abbas a map and package involving roughly 93–97% of the WB with 1:1 land swaps, Gaza, and a special regime for the Holy Basin. Abbas Rejected.  

●Trump “Peace to Prosperity”plan, 2020: The PA rejected the plan outright
