text:
I had a conversation tonight about the Lindsay Clancy trial with the most reasonable and levelheaded woman in the world, my mother.

Only a day before, one of the most honest conversations I ever had with my father, where I was able to forgive him and receive his forgiveness.

And after experiencing a week of divine intervention and premonitions.

I was granted a vision of our doom and most importantly our escape from it.  

Let me first congratulate all who are here now and those who will come to bear witness to what is about to happen. 

Just know your ancestors are proud of you and your progeny will celebrate this moment forever. 

You are in one of the most important moments in humanities' history and have earned front row seats to bear witness to God's might, grace, forgiveness and love. 

My intention with this post will be to heal each of you of an affliction that has directed humanities existence since Cain and Abel, and the moment Adam had betrayed Eve and the moment they both betrayed God. 

The same affliction that has brought us to this point in history where everything seems inevitable and doomed. 

Why it feels like World War 3 is right around the corner. 

So many "whys" I will try my best to answer with the best way we know of... with storytelling.

I have been blessed with an opportunity of providing to the world and each individual the miraculous means to heal from our fallen nature and our doom. 

A nature we invited in and God had to enforce, because it was absolutely necessary and because he loves us. 

A nature that we tricked ourselves into, believing it to be a game.

I found the Garden of Eden and I am proud to say we are living in it.

We are simply blind to it from ego. 

Please realize that the ego is not a good or bad thing.

It is ultimately how we map out reality to assess threats. 

But it is because of this we have made threats of ourselves, each other, each person, yourself and others.

We might have fallen, but today is the day we rise with Christ for he has risen me and all of us to this very moment.

I am going to reason with you, and I want you to walk this path with me like I have with Christ and God's grace.

In order to do this requires faith, humility, forgiveness and storytelling. 

It also requires me to address you directly, dear reader. What you will read will heal you. I know it will and it's why I must do it. I want you to prosper. I want you to know I love you. For this reason I you want to bear witness that Christ and God love you. 

I need you to forgive me if I sound unreasonable, but it is for this very reason, and Reason itself, that I will do what is necessary and you will read because I assure you, you must. 

If we wish to be reasonable and within reason, first, I need to ask you to do something that I know may sound completely unreasonable. 

Forgive yourself and those who you know need it. 

All transgressions and all mistakes you have made and has been done against you were just variables that molded you into the individual you are to be here, now, reading this. 

Everyone else you know and have known is a part of this with you, both of the past and to be remembered into the future and beyond. 

They deserve the same courtesy of forgiveness that you have granted yourself for reading this.

Please though make sure to forgive yourself. 

I want you to heal and Jesus does to. 

As I type this I have a reverberating energy emanating around me, God's grace helping me write this.

What you will learn will shock you.

Please though remember while you read this God's most repeated command in The Bible while reading this:

Do not be afraid.

I was afraid to once I realized the mission God has sent me on.

Also remember the moment Moses asked God what his name was so he could guide and free the slaves of Egypt, 

"I AM WHO I AM"

Take a deep breath and exhale and say it once to yourself for yourself. 

If you feel that is to vain, don't worry God understands that to and he scoffs with you. 

Come as you are. 

This is a day to seize and let come what may.

We are made in God's image. Remember this.

 He will be there with you every step of the way to catch you as I guide you.

You, me, him, with Christ as our messenger, translator and mender are experiencing this universe together.

He is with you every step of the way and you will find your way out of this.

I have been tasked to be a guide on a perfect convergence of individual will, spontaneous and cooperation, and what can be simply explained as luck.

Luck being a combination of God's divine intervention delivered as symmetry and coincidence and happenstance. 

What I hope to do for those of you who don't believe is realize this redemption comes at a simple cost.

Forgive yourself and come as you are.

I am just a man who has made many mistakes and committed my fair share of wrongs.

For every typo you have made, let this be the redemption.

I have fallen like the rest of you, and I just happen to have gotten back up from the deepest of falls and have arrived first to the Garden by sheer coincidence, by God's hand and by some of the most intuitive people on Earth. 

What I will call the 5th Estate.

First, let me introduce who I am so you understand what I mean by a perfect convergence of individual will, spontaneous cooperation, luck and God's divine intervention.

My name is "Michael Boulton" a name that has never been truly my own, but I was still glad to have.

I would like to thank Michael Bolton and Mike Judge for their contribution in this effort. Without their talent I wouldn't be here today. 

Because of sheer coincidence I had to juggle my ego in a way most people did not. 

First, as some of you have probably guessed, my name brought me a bit of mockery, a bit of fun and many laughs to go around.

I have had the unfortunately fortunate experience to have this motif so many bind their ego to, that then tells them their worth to the outside the world as if it's a price tag. 

In short, I have lived with the constant question, what is in a name?

Always open to different interpretations, juggling which one did I find fitting. 

Well, that changed the day I understood the true meaning to my name that eventually found me to my true purpose and why I write this today.

Michael also means "Who is God?" 

God's angel Michael struck me from the very page I learned this, as I read it. 

But in a way that will serve as proof that God is truly not only more knowledgeable and loving than we can imagine. 

He has the greatest sense of humor. 

I became an atheist.

I liked my name for the first time in irony. As my own joke on the joke that was my name. 

This happened shortly after I had graduated high school. 

Then shortly after that I found myself being poisoned at a house party where I had bummed a cigarette.

I should've known better the guy had the typical markings of someone you shouldn't accept offers like that. 

To explain it simply I overdosed. I arrived at the hospital and my heart was beating so off that I had my heart stopped to be restarted. 

The doctors couldn't tell me what it was that sent me there. What them and the police concluded was that it was likely laced with PCP or some kind of deliriant.

In that moment I had my heart stopped I came face to face with God and he gave me an option to refuse my life or refuse my death. 

I recognize the choice itself was he one last gift to me and chance to grab me before I truly fell into the abyss.

The choice was freewill at it's most naked and true form. 

One I wish I appreciated much sooner, but it is by sheer dumb luck, my dumb luck, that I arrived there. And his divine intervention that showed me that the human condition and what it means to be human, survives and thrives because of freewill. 

Freewill does this because it is God's greatest gift to us.

Apart of the reason why I have been blessed to be the first to the Garden is the very nature of my name, my rejection of God, being betrayed in the most vicious way a person could do to another and then being resurrected by his blessing of being impressed upon the meaning of what it is to be human. 

It came with a duty and mission. For being blessed with this knowledge came at the cost of being even more alienated from the world than I was. My brain though was supercharged as I experienced synesthesia and with my awareness of free will gave me determination. 

My duty was driven by fear of what God may do to me if I covet this gift and awareness. I told everyone and anyone I could knowing how this experience had saved me. What I didn't understand though was what I intuitively understood was not what people were ready to hear.

I didn't understand this at first because I didn't understand that I needed to become a storyteller. I had come off as arrogant, deceptive and brash to those around me as they didn't understand me and I failed to understand they desperately wanted to.

I did not appreciate people how they were and it was from how I perceived God for so long. This has caused so many misunderstandings. As a result I became a awful story teller to myself. 

Eventually through meditation, healing, singing and writing I became disciplined. Constantly reminded of the image God imprinted on me to bear witness to my miraculous resurrection so that the world may know that willful survival is human survival.

What I discovered was my intuition had been brought to a state of awareness and communication that I could sense people on a level that I will remain calling intuition. 

I can tell you the sensation I walk with is as if my there are angel wings on my back. This sensation I carry made me realize why so many angels get represented with wings.

Functionally its best understood as an antenna.

The more you are a master of this antenna the greater the sensation. This last week it has been more noticeable than I ever had in my life.

My ability let me see my own mask as it reflected back on people's. Every emotional connection I have is so intense. I had to as a part of my mission was take on a duty of discipline to put simply, become a storyteller.

Once God gave me the story of a literal lifetime. I became angry people didn't take it seriously. 

I took this seriously by first getting serious and then too serious and then not being taken seriously at all. Eventually finding a way to juggle the comedy, drama, tragedy, and the romantic that comes with being imbued with God's love in an undeniable way. 

Every time I tried to forget, God compelled me forward and catching me at me lowest.

What I didn't realize though and what I have come to discover is the convergence of God's will, spontaneous order, and luck.

To keep me humble God only let me come to just how important my mission was piece by piece, step by step.

First I learned to sing to get better control of my voice.

While doing this I dove into every philosophical and religious text I could find to help me explain and understand myself.

Eventually, I came to the conclusion how I would spread this Jubilee of freewill was through writing a general treatise of the Human Condition. Then I realized instead I would make it a Treatise in Defense of The Human Condition. I would name this mission of mine Ama-gi.

Ama-gi is the first word from world history we know of to mean freedom and it was for this reason I appreciated it. I also later came to appreciate it even more when I learned while working at Cato Institute that it meant "Return to Mother" and was a Ancient Sumerian legal practice of manumission where a slave freed themselves by proving they could sublimate their own hunger. 

Could they feed themselves and once fed, could they maintain? If so, they were made free. Once they could renunciate their dependency and embrace their intuition, get their wings, they became a free individual. I felt God made me go through my Ama-gi so I could tell you today to also get yours.

Along the way as I sculpted Ama-gi, I kept having insight after insight. I kept trying to work in jobs as I could and to the best of my ability. A lot of my time I spent thinking about my Ama-gi. I never forgo an opportunity to try sharpen my conversation skills and my skills as a storyteller. 

Eventually Covid-19 occurs and we all remember how that was like so I won't bore you with that part of my life, although it is important to what I will be telling you. Once you understand, so much will make sense and this is the very nature of this blessing I am being made into a vessel for today.

I realized I need to stop observing and start getting serious again. 

I began writing and typing my stories. See I figured the best way to reach people was through storytelling. I also came to the idea of doing a podcast called The 5th Estate. Due to life circumstances, I never got there, but I still wrote. Before this I wrote to, but always kept it inside my head.

Shortly after my time at the Cato Institute in 2011, I went to work at Amazon Web Services and got to physically touch some of the servers that Edward Snowden likely had remoted into at some point. I also was made aware of to the lengths that the US government had gone to manipulate the population. 

The datacenter had many of their servers running what could only be described as bot traffic to Barack Obama's and Justin Bieber's Twitter profile pages. I came to discover this myself when I was tasked as a data center technician to replace NIC cards in server racks for both the CIA and NSA. There was a number of other important systems that I don't need to mention here. Once I got replacing the equipment and fixing it, it was considered best practice to verify it worked. Well, I did and it showed me the traffic to Twitter. To private servers that had no unique identify names. Unusual, they either were considered Amazon production or used by a customer and the customer's name would be in the server. I asked coworkers and came to discover the true nature of what I was looking at. 

It sent me into an awareness of how exposed we are on the internet. I realized I would need to form my Ama-gi and my stories mostly in my head. I learned about the different programs from coworkers and then later Snowden about how they scan the internet. I already assumed on a certain level my words and ability of language had been affected by what I experienced and that I was already likely being surveilled for this very reason. I scaled back my presence on the internet. I also made sure to still speak true, but in a heightened and sometimes overtly dramatic and manic tone to through off the scanners. I figured practically it helped with my writing ability to. It did come at the cost of some opportunities I am sure, but I knew I need to be disciplined with myself, but also who I was with.

I had then learned about Fifth Generational Warfare and decided to become all I could describe as a one-man intelligence agency. I had started reading into mimetic analysis, Carl Jung on symbols and psychology. I figured if I was going to write fictional stories, while working on the story of a lifetime and Ama-gi, I could at least chisel away at the Tower of Babel with some well-crafted memes. After a bit I started seeing how memes spread from different hot zones, mainly 4chan, then make their way to Reddit, then through the different social media sites. 

All the while working, writing, memeing and arguing on the internet to better understand how to tell of Ama-gi.

Then I went into a very revealing and freighting part of my life realizing how much of entertainment and media had these symbols in them that operated like memes and went back thousands of years. Learning about how these were sometimes used to hide all sorts of things in "plain sight". I also had been made aware from a volunteer job as a forum moderator about how to spot child porn if it was being exchanged. The training included a link to the FBI's handbook on it which listed symbols. 

Then the day came when surfing on r/TheDonald during 2016 that I was memeing with others. The energy of the place was truly amazing to behold on a mimetic level. A big part of Donald Trump's win for 2016 and the media uproar against it was in response to this incredibly vibrant community. Then the Podesta and Clinton emails dropped. Suddenly the place became the most important place in world history up to that moment. I could recognize it as such; I'm sure others did.

Then one day someone posts about this weird email involving a "Pizza related map" and other odd use of words involving food. I casually post, not putting any thought into it, how people who exchange child porn would use symbols and code words to signal to each other. One of these signals was "cheese pizza". I even put a link up to a copy similar to the one I had saw explaining and showing more of these symbols. The next few posts people were putting pictures together to be shared. I went to bed and woke up the next day to Pizzagate being the subject of focus.

Suddenly I realized I had done something that I couldn't undo and I need to help at least so the fire I just started doesn't get hijacked or grow into something it shouldn't. I suddenly need to become a meme keeper of sorts. I made sure to keep informing people and trying to snip frayed rabbit holes by nipping what I thought could be psyops or communists/nazis trying to promote a cause. This kept my focus on politics, memes and the news like never before. 

I still tried to have a social life, but feeling like the man who started Pizzagate I felt obligated. Especially if I was hoping to create my path to Ama-gi and share it. I knew the one benefit this meme had above all else was it made everyone stop making idols out of other humans. Suddenly people were being made aware of just human and inhuman the world was becoming.

I felt like this country was going in a great direction, but then to watch what happened to Trump. with Russian Collusion accusations and everything else. I had no idea the enormity of the problem of globalism and just how pernicious it got. I was glad to stop hearing every voice in politics sound like Obama. Again, my sensitivity to language and communication meant every person I met who wanted to be taken seriously came to start sounding like Obama in some way. Trump for all his faults did the world of favor of breaking up the hypnotizing nature of it. It invoked a lot of false authority into everyone who used it, willingly or otherwise, that led to a lot acceptance of bureaucracy and policy as "reasonable".

Then comes Covid-19. I got a "heads up" of the virus because people were talking about it on 4chan and it spreading. Before this I had a conversation at work with coworkers about virus pandemics and I mentioned to them I thought they would be coming from a communist country first. So I paid close attention when showed up on 4chan months before the shutdowns occurred. I felt like at the time it was just a lucky prediction, like so much of my life I figured was luck, freewill and divine mission from God to give people the license to be fruitful and multiple. 

I ended up getting fired from that job and picking up a new work from home job, one week before lockdowns occurred. Funny thing was I thought it may had been a scam, then I was hired out of desperate need and was shown the job. I was convinced it was "safe". Then a little while after the lockdowns the business got way too many applicants. This allowed me though to get away from in person office politics and really focus on keeping focused on my writing, studying and memekeeping. I also kept predicting things. Again I thought it was luck and intuition. 

As my life was tossed and turned with Covid like everyone else I was doing well with my job. Then the BLM riots started. The job I had I was helping out accountants who used Quickbooks and Sage. I became a manager in short order for the customer support team because of my abilities and was a very good teacher. I really prided myself on this and I wanted to really make the company something special. Some of the clients we had though were critical to the Democrat and Leftist nonprofits and political funding. 

I remember helping a lady with a problem. She was very persistent and would take over the mouse whenever I stopped to research something. She told me she had to process some funds. I remember the way she was doing it and every time it was the same exact amount. I was witnessing what felt like to me fraud and it was going to BLM organizations. I remember one account she sent money to, the organization was on my other screen being mentioned in the article I was reading. I once again found my staring face to face with another giant scam and was inadvertently contributing to something that to me was so immoral with my abilities. I lost a lot of motivation and became increasingly agitated as I noticed how many of these organizations were on our network. I lost that job and continued my journey.

Still working on my writing, on the story of a lifetime and Ama-gi and trying to keep to the meme of Pizzagate. I kept predicting odd things and having more and more odd coincidences. I was remembering Carl Jung's take on symmetry being God's way of talking to you. And I never forgot this. Slowly my mission changed from luck to what felt like more and more reasons for me to keep going and keep trying. God beckoning me forward. 

At this point I had a dozen or so stories in various stages of completion and one shared universe. I had come up with the idea to have it start out as two separate series. One sci-fi, the other fantasy. In the sci-fi series there would be a A Song of Ice and Fire/Game of Thrones level of different stories that would converge into a maelstrom that would lead to the apocalypse. 

Then the fantasy series would have a story similar to Lord of the Rings where they discover what happened in the sci-fi series. Basically, AI had come to rule everything and the last man to have freewill would recognize the unusual situation he was in. Eventually he started going mad and read The Bible coming to the Book of Revelations recognizing he was the anti-Christ. 

He is redeemed when he realizes he still has the ability to shut off the machine. Telling himself that it had to be done to give humanity another chance. In doing so he recognizes himself also as the second coming of Christ. As the AI started dissipating the world goes into cataclysm. All the while the AI rapidly imbued itself into the Earth as if to upgrade the biological reality of Gaia. Then it gave birth to "magic" that would exist in the fantasy series.

Anyone I had chance to tell this to thought it was fucking genius and I was proud of myself for getting so many original ideas for more stories. I am now up to 30 in various stages of completion. But building to stories to be able to lead to this amazing flip in series was what kept me going to write stories to lead to The Architek.

All the while still studying, still memeing, still learning what I could. I tried to socialize the best I could, but by the time Covid rolled around that limited things. I already was a hermit, but now I saw it as a shield with whatever was occurring. The more things were unfolding I could see the despair and worry in people's faces. I kept to myself realizing I would be helping matters if I talked too much of doom and gloom. Mainly I had grown so comfortable with talking about conspiracy theories I noticed that this would worry others. 

I decided to move back in with my mom in her new place and help her settle in. I had been fired once again from another job, likely because of my wanting to talk about what was happening in the news. People would be worried and, in my attempts, to talk them through it I didn't realize I was pushing them away. The conspiracy around the world I was seeing on the internet was on my doorstep. I decided I would just go live with my mom and focus on writing, start a podcast, and push Ama-gi out to the world.

At this point in my life, I should mention my luck became more and more of a drive to do something, anything. The amount of coincidence, symmetry and predictions I was making keep pushing me and beckoning me forward. Never forgetting about my mission. 

I decided to show up on X after being on no social media and minimizing my use for years. Multiple times clearing out web browsing data, making new accounts and trying to throw anyone off my trail.

I had formulated and worked on a number of things as away to introduce myself to the world. First I came to realize the storytelling, from the days of sitting around to the campfire to sitting around the monitor and sitting around the global campfire of the internet, memes were the stories. I figured how could I get the team together. There was so many times I tried reaching out to people and posting things but it was either too much or not enough.

11 Essential Supply Chain Stories for Procurement Leaders
https://t.co/ZBfYd7PRPB

According to Press Monitor's tracking of Indian publications, this media monitoring report delivers 11 essential stories on news on supply chain and procurement. The press review draws on print media monitoring data to provide media intelligence on the developments shaping India's logistics and defence landscape.

1. PM Modi Inaugurates 35,000 Crore Projects in Vadodara
A front-page report in Deccan Chronicle says Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated sections of the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor in Vadodara, Gujarat, on 8 September. Highlighting an investment of over rupees thirty five thousand crore, he praised rapid infrastructure execution while dismissing opposition criticism. Additionally, India is working toward a joint statement at the Brics summit to advance diplomatic consensus on regional conflicts.
Why it matters: Prime Minister Narendra Modi's inauguration of over 35,000 crore rupees in development projects, including the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor, marks a defining moment for Indian infrastructure and supply chain connectivity.
Key detail: The 1,506-kilometre corridor links JNPT with Dadri, with double-stack container services already operational from Mumbai to Vadodara, carrying goods equivalent to over 250 trucks per train.
Source: Economic Times, Asian Age, Indian Express, and 4 other publications.
Next step: Track how the DFC impacts logistics costs for manufacturers and exporters in the coming quarters.

2. Saudi Energy Facilities Halt Following Strikes
A front-page report in Business Line says Saudi Arabia halted several key energy facilities after Iran-backed Houthi militants claimed fresh missile and drone strikes on sites near the Yemen border. The attacks, which targeted Aramco infrastructure in Abha, Najran and Jazan, have ignited fires and injured over seventy individuals while raising fears of prolonged supply disruptions that are pushing Brent crude prices toward one hundred dollars a barrel. Market analysts warn that ongoing hostilities, compounded by heightened Iran-United States tensions and restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz, could sustain shipping blockades well into twenty twenty seven.
Why it matters: Houthi missile and drone strikes on Saudi Aramco infrastructure have halted key energy facilities and wounded over 70 people, pushing Brent crude toward 100 dollars a barrel and threatening global supply chains.
Key detail: Fires at critical oil infrastructure in Abha, Najran, and Jazan threaten prolonged supply disruptions that could extend well into 2027.
Source: Business Line, The Pioneer.
Next step: Monitor how supply chain disruptions in the Red Sea and Strait of Hormuz affect global freight routing and commodity prices.

3. 21.10 Lakh Crore Defence Procurement Approved
A front-page report in Deccan Chronicle says the Defence Acquisition Council has approved procurement proposals totalling 21.10 lakh crore for India’s Army, Navy and Air Force. The acquisitions cover critical capabilities including battlefield mobility, electronic warfare, aviation and chemical biological radiological nuclear reconnaissance systems while emphasising indigenous manufacturing to bolster domestic defence infrastructure. Officials stress that timely execution without cost escalation is essential to bridge operational gaps and enhance national security posture.
Why it matters: The Defence Acquisition Council's approval of procurement proposals totalling 21.10 lakh crore for the Army, Navy, and Air Force signals a major boost for India's defence-industrial base and indigenous manufacturing ecosystem.
Key detail: Acquisitions cover battlefield mobility, electronic warfare, aviation, and chemical biological radiological nuclear reconnaissance systems, with 98 percent expected from domestic manufacturers.
Source: Deccan Chronicle.
Next step: Watch for domestic manufacturer announcements and defence stock movements in the coming weeks.

4. 73,000 Crore Freight Corridor
A front-page report in Business Standard says the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor will cost rupees seventy-three thousand crore, deliver a cost saving of six to seven percent compared with single‑stack container trains, and reduce travel time by over sixty percent between Dadri and JNPA versus conventional routes. The corridor’s key advantage is the ability to double‑stack containers at JNPA, a major export‑import hub, and similar services already run from ports such as Mundra and Pipavav. Each double‑stack train can carry the equivalent of twenty‑five thousand trucks, boosting freight capacity.
Why it matters: The Western Dedicated Freight Corridor's cost structure and capacity advantages position it as a transformative logistics infrastructure project for India's export-import sector.
Key detail: Each double-stack train carries the equivalent of 25,000 trucks, delivering a 6 to 7 percent cost saving and reducing travel time by over 60 percent between Dadri and JNPA.
Source: Business Standard.
Next step: Assess how double-stack operations at JNPA and Mundra will reshape export logistics and supply chain costs.

5. Defence Index Hits Record High
A front-page report in Business Line says the Defence Acquisition Council approved capital acquisition proposals worth around 1.1 lakh crore rupees, causing defence stocks to rally on Tuesday. The Nifty Defence index soared to a record high of 10,030.65 before closing at 9,998.70, with about 98 percent of procurement expected from domestic manufacturers. Jefferies initiated buy ratings on Solar Industries and Astro Microwave, while Kotak Securities identified Bharat Electronics Limited and Hindustan Aeronautics Limited as key beneficiaries.
Why it matters: The Nifty Defence index reaching a record high of 10,030.65 reflects market confidence in India's defence procurement pipeline and the government's push for indigenous manufacturing.
Key detail: About 98 percent of the 1.1 lakh crore in capital acquisition proposals is expected from domestic manufacturers, with Jefferies and Kotak Securities identifying key beneficiaries.
Source: Business Line.
Next step: Follow defence stock performance as procurement contracts are awarded and executed.

6. Rs 73,000 Crore Western DFC Opens
A front-page report in Business Standard says Prime Minister Narendra Modi dedicated the Rs 73,000 crore Western Dedicated Freight Corridor to the nation on 8 September in New Delhi. The 2,800 km corridor connects Dadri in Uttar Pradesh with Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority and is expected to cut freight transit time by about 60 per cent. The project, first proposed by former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee, links northern industrial centres with major ports including Mundra, Kandla, Pipavav and JNPA.
Why it matters: Prime Minister Narendra Modi's dedication of the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor underscores the government's commitment to reducing logistics costs and improving supply chain efficiency across India.
Key detail: The 2,800 km corridor connects Dadri in Uttar Pradesh with JNPA, linking northern industrial centres with major ports including Mundra, Kandla, and Pipavav.
Source: Business Standard.
Next step: Evaluate the corridor's impact on reducing logistics costs for businesses relying on port connectivity and inland freight movement.

7. India Eyes SACU Preferential Trade Pact
A front-page report in Business Standard says India has signed terms of reference to launch negotiations for a preferential trade agreement with the Southern African Customs Union. Signed on 12 August by officials from New Delhi and the five-nation bloc, the pact aims to conclude within a year while focusing initially on goods to explore commercial complementarities without sweeping tariff cuts. The diplomatic initiative marks a strategic pivot towards developing markets to diversify export destinations and secure critical mineral supply chains amid global economic uncertainty.
Why it matters: India's launch of preferential trade negotiations with the Southern African Customs Union marks a strategic pivot towards developing markets, diversifying export destinations and securing critical mineral supply chains.
Key detail: The pact aims to conclude within a year, focusing initially on goods to explore commercial complementarities without sweeping tariff cuts.
Source: Business Standard.
Next step: Monitor how the SACU pact diversifies India's export destinations and strengthens mineral supply chain resilience.

8. Rs 38 Crore Churu Bridge Tender
A front-page report in The Hindu says the Rajasthan Public Works Department has invited bids for constructing a two-lane road over bridge near Churu. The engineering procurement construction project on State Highway 07C carries an approximate value of 38.14 crores. Bidding concludes at six o'clock pm on 22 September 2026.
Why it matters: The Rajasthan Public Works Department's invitation for bids on a major road over bridge near Churu reflects the ongoing expansion of India's highway infrastructure network.
Key detail: The engineering procurement construction project on State Highway 07C carries an approximate value of 38.14 crores, with bidding concluding on 22 September 2026.
Source: The Hindu.
Next step: Track EPC contractors bidding on this and similar Rajasthan infrastructure projects for supply chain opportunities.

9. Tenders Announced: 12 Railway Projects
A front‑page report in Deccan Chronicle says Indian Railways has issued twelve tender notices for a variety of railway equipment and services, including over‑riding curved switches, LED emergency light units, thick web switch expansions, Jalvaayu A‑Q‑U‑A gas generators, hydraulic presses and underground signalling cables, with opening dates on twenty‑five July and locations spanning Assam, West Bengal and other NFR regions.
Why it matters: Indian Railways' issuance of twelve tender notices for equipment and services signals continued investment in railway infrastructure and the growing procurement pipeline for suppliers.
Key detail: Tenders cover over-riding curved switches, LED emergency light units, gas generators, hydraulic presses, and underground signalling cables, with opening dates on 25 July across Assam, West Bengal, and other NFR regions.
Source: Deccan Chronicle.
Next step: Identify suppliers positioned to win these railway procurement contracts and prepare for compliance requirements.

10. 8 Tender Items for Indian Railways
A front-page report in Deccan Chronicle says the Principal Chief Material Manager of North Eastern Railway, on behalf of the President of India, invites tenders through an e-procurement system for the supply of various railway items including insulated rail joints, fishplates, and crossings in Gorakhpur. The tender notices were issued on 7 September 2026 with deadlines ranging from October to November 2026 for items such as derailing switches, turnout components, and automotive sealant.
Why it matters: The North Eastern Railway's tender for insulated rail joints, fishplates, crossings, and other components highlights the ongoing need for quality railway infrastructure supplies across India's northeastern network.
Key detail: Tender notices were issued on 7 September 2026 from Gorakhpur, with deadlines ranging from October to November 2026 for items including derailing switches and turnout components.
Source: Deccan Chronicle.
Next step: Watch for e-procurement registration surges as suppliers prepare to bid on these railway items.

11. Northeast Frontier Railway E-Procurement Tender
A front-page report in Deccan Chronicle says that E-Procurement Tender Notice No O4/2O24 has been issued by the Principal Chief Materials Manager of the Northeast Frontier Railway in Maligaon. The tender invites bids for the manufacture, supply, installation, commissioning and testing of Sports Utility Vehicle and Light Commercial Vehicle based Rail cum Road Inspection Vehicles according to RDSO specifications, with a dated submission deadline of 24 September 2026. Prospective bidders must log on to the IREPS website and submit their offers electronically, using a Class-III Digital Signature Certificate if they are not already registered.
Why it matters: The NFR's e-procurement tender for Rail cum Road Inspection Vehicles reflects the digitization of Indian railway procurement and the growing emphasis on technology-driven inspection capabilities.
Key detail: Bidders must submit offers electronically via the IREPS website using a Class-III Digital Signature Certificate, with a submission deadline of 24 September 2026.
Source: Deccan Chronicle.
Next step: Prepare for the digital submission process and RDSO compliance requirements ahead of the deadline.

Closing: With defence procurement at record levels, freight corridors reshaping logistics, and new trade pacts expanding India's global reach, how will your supply chain strategy adapt to India's infrastructure revolution?

According to Press Monitor's tracking of Indian publications, this press review delivers 17 essential election stories that capture the full spectrum of India's electoral landscape. This media intelligence report draws on print media monitoring across national and regional outlets to bring you today's most consequential news on elections — from Punjab's factional battles to Delhi's voter roll controversies.

1. Sachin Pilot Outlines Punjab Congress Strategy
A front-page report in Asian Age says Congress leadership in-charge Sachin Pilot met Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi in New Delhi on Tuesday to address internal party rifts and finalise strategies for the upcoming Punjab Assembly elections. The discussions focused on uniting warring factions within the state unit and preparing a robust campaign roadmap to challenge the ruling Aam Aadmi Party and other opposition groups. Pilot pledged his full commitment to strengthening organisational unity and protecting farmers and youth rights across the state.
Sachin Pilot's meeting with Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra in New Delhi signals a unified front for the Congress party ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections. Why it matters: The strategy session could reshape opposition dynamics in the state. Key detail: Pilot pledged to protect farmers and youth rights while uniting warring factions. Source: Asian Age, 8 September. What comes next: Watch for Pilot's next public move to consolidate the Punjab unit. How will the Aam Aadmi Party respond to this opposition alignment?

2. Raghav Chadha's Name Appears In Delhi Voter List
A front-page report in The Hindu says Party MP Raghav Chadha's name was included in the electoral roll of the Rajinder Nagar Assembly constituency in Delhi even as poll officials rejected the claim. AAP Delhi president Saurabh Bharadwaj accused the Election Commission of fraud at a press conference, questioning how Mr. Chadha became the seventy-fourth-seventh voter when there were seven hundred forty-six voters in the draft roll. The Delhi Chief Electoral Officer stated that over twenty-five thousand Form Six applications are under process and actual additions will be published on November four.
AAP MP Raghav Chadha's name appeared in Delhi's electoral roll despite poll officials rejecting the claim, sparking fraud allegations. Why it matters: The controversy raises serious questions about electoral integrity in the capital. Key detail: Chadha became the 747th voter when the draft roll listed 746 names. Source: The Hindu. What comes next: The Delhi Chief Electoral Officer confirmed over 25,000 Form 6 applications are under process. Will the Election Commission address these concerns before the November 4 final list?

3. Congress Sends Sachin Pilot to Punjab
A front-page report in Asian Age says Sachin Pilot has been appointed Congress general secretary in-charge of Punjab ahead of early next year polls. The party faces factionalism between Charanjit Singh Channi and Amrinder Singh Raja Warring, while the BJP has sent Satish Poonia to build its base. The Aam Aadmi Party, which won in 2022, now battles incumbency as Congress seeks to unite diverse voter blocs.
Sachin Pilot's appointment as Congress general secretary in-charge of Punjab marks a strategic push to reclaim the state in 2027. Why it matters: Punjab's electoral battlefield now features a three-way contest between Congress, AAP, and BJP. Key detail: Pilot faces the challenge of bridging factional divides between Charanjit Singh Channi and Amrinder Singh Raja Warring. Source: Asian Age. What comes next: The party must balance factional interests while building a coherent campaign narrative. Can Congress overcome its internal divisions in time for the polls?

4. BJP Focuses on Weak Booths in Rajasthan Civic Polls
A front-page report in New Indian Express says political activities surrounding Rajasthan's municipal elections have reached a fever pitch, with voting for 309 urban local bodies scheduled in two phases on September 9 and 11. The BJP has identified weak booths and activated its network of party workers to ensure supporters turn out to vote, while the Congress is reaching out to independent candidates who may not be strong enough to win but could cut into the vote share of its candidates. Chief Minister Bhajan Lal Sharma has thrown himself into the campaign, holding roadshows and public meetings across the state, while former Chief Minister Ashok Gehlot and BJP leader Gajendra Singh Shekhawat have also been active in the contest.
The BJP has identified weak booths across Rajasthan's 309 urban local bodies and activated its party worker network ahead of the September 9 and 11 voting phases. Why it matters: Municipal elections often serve as a barometer for state-level political sentiment. Key detail: Chief Minister Bhajan Lal Sharma has been holding roadshows while the Congress targets independent candidates to split opposition votes. Source: New Indian Express. What comes next: The two-phase voting will reveal whether BJP's booth-level strategy translates into seats. Will the Congress independent candidate strategy pay off?

5. BJP Juggles Caste Equations Ahead of 2027 UP Polls
A front-page report in Statesman says the Bharatiya Janata Party is juggling caste equations ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh polls. The party is strategizing to address caste dynamics to secure electoral success.
The Bharatiya Janata Party is navigating complex caste dynamics as it prepares for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. Why it matters: UP is India's largest state electorate and a bellwether for national politics. Key detail: The party's caste balancing act involves communities such as Yadavs, Kurmis, and Sainis. Source: Statesman. What comes next: How BJP resolves internal debates over caste representation will define its poll readiness.

A front-page report in Statesman says the Bharatiya Janata Party has restructured its executive teams across six regions of Uttar Pradesh to prepare for the twenty twenty seven state assembly elections. The delayed appointments have sparked internal debates over caste balance and geographical representation, particularly affecting communities such as Yadavs, Kurmis, and Sainis. The BJP has restructured its executive teams across six regions of Uttar Pradesh, triggering internal debates over caste balance and geographical representation. Key detail: Veteran workers and local leaders have voiced dissatisfaction over perceived exclusions and shifted power dynamics within the newly formed committees. Source: Statesman, Lucknow, 8 September. What comes next: The delayed appointments may fuel further internal friction. Will the new committees deliver the unity BJP needs?

7. Election Commission Delays Two Lok Sabha By-Elections
A front-page report in The Pioneer says that the Election Commission has scheduled a parliamentary by-election for the Nagaon constituency in Assam to take place on October 6, with counting on October 9. Polls for the Basirhat seat in West Bengal and the Shillong seat in Meghalaya remain delayed due to a pending high court election petition and an ongoing revision of electoral rolls. The Nagaon seat became vacant after MP Pradyut Bordoloi resigned following a successful state assembly campaign, while a legal challenge for Basirhat continues despite the incumbent's death in September.
The Election Commission has scheduled a by-election for Nagaon in Assam on October 6, while Basirhat and Shillong remain delayed. 8. AfD Wins Key German State Election
A front-page report in Times of India says the Alternative for Germany party secured a significant victory in the Saxony-Anhalt state election, intensifying concerns over the growing influence of far-right movements across the continent. While anti-immigrant and pro-Russian factions have gained substantial ground recently, analysts note that mainstream consolidation, coalition building, and notable electoral defeats for populist figures demonstrate that the political shift remains unpredictable rather than linear.
The Alternative for Germany party secured a significant victory in the Saxony-Anhalt state election, intensifying concerns over far-right influence in Europe. 9. TVK Faces First Electoral Test In October
A front-page report in The Hans India says TVK will face its first major electoral test in October during upcoming by-elections in Tamil Nadu. Writer K Sakunthala argues that the state's mature electorate requires the party to prove its credibility through clear policies on jobs, education, healthcare, and state rights, rather than relying on celebrity influence. 10. Congress Unites Leadership Ahead Of Punjab Polls
A front-page report in Hindustan Times says Congress general secretary Sachin Pilot has secured assurances of unity from senior party leaders in Punjab ahead of the upcoming assembly elections. Following his recent appointment as the state leader, Pilot met with former chief minister and party member of parliament Charanjit Singh Channi, who pledged full support for the Congress election campaign. Both leaders are focused on consolidating internal backing to strengthen the party's electoral prospects in the region.
Congress general secretary Sachin Pilot has secured assurances of unity from senior party leaders in Punjab ahead of the upcoming assembly elections. Why it matters: Internal cohesion is critical for any party challenging the incumbent Aam Aadmi Party. Key detail: Former chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi pledged full support for the Congress election campaign. Source: Hindustan Times. What comes next: The unity pledge will be tested as the campaign intensifies. Can Congress translate backstage solidarity into votes?

11. Akhilesh Yadav Launches Student Campaign
A front-page report in Statesman says that Samajwadi Party National President Akhilesh Yadav launched the Samajwadi Chhatra Sabha's student awareness campaign in Lucknow on 8 September. He announced blue uniforms for Chhatra Sabha cadres and said the campaign would connect students with socialist ideology.
Samajwadi Party National President Akhilesh Yadav launched the Samajwadi Chhatra Sabha's student awareness campaign in Lucknow. Why it matters: Engaging young voters is increasingly central to electoral success in India. Key detail: Yadav announced blue uniforms for Chhatra Sabha cadres and framed the campaign around socialist ideology. Source: Statesman, Lucknow, 8 September. What comes next: The student campaign could reshape youth political engagement in Uttar Pradesh.

12. TMC Factions Battle Bypolls
A front-page report in Hindustan Times says the two factions of the Trinamool Congress are preparing for their first electoral battle in upcoming bypolls at two West Bengal assembly seats. The Election Commission of India announced that bypolls to Rejinagar and Nandigram will be held on October 6 with results on October 9. Former minister Firhad Hakim's faction and Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee's loyalists are both vying for the party symbol while BJP leaders claim administration control could influence outcomes.
The two factions of the Trinamool Congress are preparing for their first electoral battle in upcoming bypolls at Rejinagar and Nandigram in West Bengal. Why it matters: The bypolls will test whether TMC's internal divisions have weakened its electoral base. Key detail: The Election Commission announced voting on October 6 with results on October 9. Source: Hindustan Times, Kolkata. What comes next: Both factions will vie for the party symbol while BJP claims administration influence could sway outcomes. Which TMC faction will emerge stronger?

13. Election Commission Clarifies Voter ID Rules
A front-page report in Tribune says the Election Commission clarified voters eligible for exercising their franchise during the upcoming bypolls in five Assembly constituencies in West Bengal, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry and one Lok Sabha seat in Assam on October 6 can bring any of the mandated documents, if they are not able to produce their election photo identity cards on polling day. Voters who are not able to produce EPIC can produce any one of the alternative photo identity documents including Aadhaar card, MGNREGA job card, passbooks with photograph issued by a bank or post office, Ayushman Bharat health card, driving licence, PAN card, and others.
The Election Commission clarified that voters eligible for bypolls in West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, and Assam can use alternative photo identity documents if they cannot produce their EPIC. Why it matters: The clarification ensures broader voter participation and reduces disenfranchisement risks. Key detail: Accepted documents include Aadhaar card, MGNREGA job card, bank passbooks with photograph, Ayushman Bharat health card, driving licence, and PAN card. Source: Tribune. What comes next: Voters must ensure they carry one of the mandated documents on polling day.

14. Delhi Rolls Cut One Third of Voters
A front-page report in Asian Age says a fresh audit reveals that Delhi special electoral revision has removed nearly one third of registered voters, surpassing previous assembly election winning margins in sixty eight constituencies. Following the February twenty twenty five polls, authorities identified over forty seven lakh additional individuals as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate, prompting activists to question the legitimacy of the electoral outcomes. To address displacement from recent demolitions, the chief electoral officer also confirmed that affected residents may file form eight updates for inclusion in the final November voter list.
A fresh audit reveals that Delhi's special electoral revision removed nearly one third of registered voters, surpassing previous assembly election winning margins in 68 constituencies. Key detail: Over 47 lakh additional individuals were identified as absent, shifted, dead, or duplicate after the February 2025 polls. Source: Asian Age. What comes next: Affected residents may file Form 8 updates for inclusion in the final November voter list. How will this audit affect the political landscape in Delhi?

15. AIADMK Targets Two Tamil Nadu Byelections
A front-page report in New Indian Express says nominations for the Madurantakam and Dharapuram Assembly bypolls commence on Wednesday, marking a significant trial of political dominance for Tamil Nadu major parties. The ruling group aims to defend its recent successes after two legislators crossed over to the emerging third party, while seeking support from a national coalition partner. Meanwhile, the opposition looks to strengthen its standing by targeting at least one win or a top two finish in both races.
Nominations for the Madurantakam and Dharapuram Assembly bypolls mark a significant trial of political dominance for Tamil Nadu's major parties. Why it matters: The bypolls will test whether the ruling group can defend its recent successes after two legislators crossed over to an emerging third party. Key detail: The opposition aims to secure at least one win or a top two finish in both races. Source: New Indian Express. What comes next: The bypoll results could reshape the balance of power in the Tamil Nadu assembly.

16. Trump Faces Senate Loss
A front-page report in Business Line says that after the 2020 election, Republicans were poised to hold the Senate majority if they won just one of two Georgia runoff races, but President Trump turned the races into a referendum on his claims of stolen votes, leading to Democratic wins in both seats and a 50‑seat majority under Vice President Kamala Harris’s tie‑breaking vote. The story also notes that several key Senate races across states such as Alaska, Ohio, Texas, Iowa, Kansas, Nebraska, Michigan and New Hampshire are now in jeopardy, with only Michigan and New Hampshire seen as pickup chances for Republicans.
After the 2020 election, Republicans were poised to hold the Senate majority if they won just one of two Georgia runoff races, but President Trump turned the races into a referendum on his claims of stolen votes. Why it matters: The outcome reshaped the balance of power in Washington and offers lessons for electoral strategies worldwide. Key detail: Democrats won both Georgia seats, giving Vice President Kamala Harris a 50-seat majority with tie-breaking vote. Source: Business Line. What comes next: Several key Senate races across Alaska, Ohio, Texas, Iowa, Kansas, Nebraska, Michigan, and New Hampshire are now in jeopardy.

17. Delhi Electoral Roll Inclusion Update
A front-page report in Tribune says the Chief Electoral Officer for Delhi has clarified that eligible voters excluded from the draft electoral rolls may still apply for inclusion until 30 September. The draft list was released on 31 August following a house-to-house enumeration exercise conducted between 30 June and 17 August. Booth-level officers must physically verify applications alongside written forms, and any deletions require strict adherence to legal procedures under the Representation of the People Act.
The Chief Electoral Officer for Delhi clarified that eligible voters excluded from the draft electoral rolls may still apply for inclusion until 30 September. Why it matters: This window ensures that no eligible voter is permanently disenfranchised during the special electoral revision. text:
BE KIND

Advice from a Retired Husband

It  is important for men to remember that, as women grow older, it becomes  harder for them to maintain the same quality of housekeeping as when  they were younger. When this becomes apparent, try not to yell at them.  Some are oversensitive, and there's nothing worse than an overly  sensitive woman.

My name is Bob. Let me relate how I handled this  situation with my wife, Rosie. When I retired a few years ago, it  became necessary for Rosie to get a full-time job, along with her  part-time job, both for extra income and for the health benefits that we  needed. Shortly after she started working, I noticed she was beginning  to show her age. I usually get home from the golf club about the same  time she gets home from work

Although she knows how hungry I am,  she almost always says she must rest for half an hour or so before she  starts dinner. I don't yell at her. Instead, I tell her to take her time  and just wake me when she gets dinner on the table.

I generally  have lunch in the Grill at the golf club, so eating out is not an option  for us in the evening. I'm ready for some home-cooked food when I walk  through that door. She used to do the dishes as soon as we finished  eating but now it's not unusual for them to sit on the table for several  hours after dinner.

I do what I can by diplomatically reminding  her several times each evening that they won't clean themselves. I know  she really appreciates this, as it does seem to motivate her to get them  done before she goes to bed.

Another symptom of aging is  complaining, I think. For example, she will say that it is difficult for  her to find time to pay the monthly bills during her lunch hour, but  guys, we take them for better or worse, so I just smile and offer  encouragement. I tell her to stretch it out over two, or even three  days. That way, she won't have to rush so much. I also remind her that  missing lunch completely now and then would help her figure. I like to  think tact is one of my strong points.

When doing simple jobs,  she seems to think she needs more rest periods. She had to take a break  when she was only half-finished mowing the lawn. I tried not to make a  scene. I'm a fair man. I told her to fix herself a nice, big, cold glass  of freshly squeezed orange juice, and just relax for a while. And, if  she is making one for herself, she might as well make one for me too.

I  know that I probably look like a saint in the way I support Rosie. I'm  not saying that showing this much patience & consideration is easy.  Many men would find it difficult if not impossible. Nobody knows better  than I do how frustrating women get as they get older. However, guys,  even if you just use a little more tact and less criticism of your  ageing wife because of reading this article, I will consider that  writing it was well worthwhile. After all, we are put on this earth to  help each other.

Bob died suddenly of a perforated rectum after  publishing this letter. The police report says he was found with a  Calloway extra-long 50-inch Big Bertha Driver II golf club jammed up his  rear end, with barely 5 inches of grip showing. A sledgehammer was  lying nearby. His wife Rosie was arrested and charged with murder. The  all-woman jury took only 9 minutes to find her "Not Guilty", accepting  her defense that Bob somehow without looking, accidentally sat down on  his golf club!

text:
Chapter Two

A Different Color of Water
The ferry had been in open water long enough that Miami was only a pale interruption behind him. Ahead, the Bahamas were not yet a line. There was only the ocean, which at this hour was not blue so much as beaten metal, and the sun, which found the side of his throat the way it had found it on the causeway and on the balcony and on every east-facing thing he had ever arranged his life around.
He said thank you without opening his mouth.
The light came into him the way it always did — not a metaphor, a meal. Heat under the skin. The flue opening. After the work in the apartment his body had been a little too precise, a little gray at the mouth, as if the night rumor had tried to climb back into a man who did not believe it. Noon on the water put him right. He sat on the starboard bench with his face turned into it and let the other passengers do what other passengers did: look at their phones, look at the wake, look anywhere except at a man taking the sun as if it had asked to be taken.
The planet was quieter. He did not stay with that thought. The ocean would not let him. Water at this angle — flat, glare-struck, going on without a church or a campo to interrupt it — had only one place to send him, and it was not last Sunday.
It was a rio in Dorsoduro in the summer of 1761, and the water then had been the color of cheap glass, green where the shade of a palazzo cut it, white where noon laid a coin on it, and the air had smelled of tar and coffee and the wet stone that Venice sweated in July.
He had gone back to the city the way a man goes back to a habit. Acre had not sent him. No line had gone loud. He had wanted an east window and a language that sat in his mouth without being a disguise, and Venice, even in her long decline — the galleys fewer, the Republic arguing with her own reflection — still knew how to throw light off water at breakfast.
The warehouse on the Zattere had needed a clerk who could read a bill of lading in more tongues than was decent. He had given them one name and three languages and hidden the rest. In the afternoons he took his cup outside because the interior of the warehouse was fasting, and because the Zattere at that hour was a long pale blade of stone aimed at the Giudecca, and the sun came down it like a thing that had been invited.
Nicolò thought he was an idiot.
That was how they met. Not a mask, not a feast-day, not a letter slipped under a door. A man of twenty-eight with coffee on his wrists and a Roman nose that had never been important to anyone, standing in the warehouse door with a sack of beans and saying, in the Venetian that made a joke of every foreigner, that only the English and the mad stood in July as if July were a friend.
“I’m not English,” he said.
“Then you’re the other thing.”
Nicolò had said it smiling. He had the kind of mouth that smiled before it had decided to. Elìa — that was the name he was wearing that year, a short thing that could pass in a warehouse — had by then already worn enough names to know the difference between a door and a trap. He took the sack so that Nicolò would have to come out into the light to take it back. They stood there longer than the sack required. Behind them the warehouse ticked and settled. In front of them the Giudecca lay like a rusty knife across the water. Nicolò squinted and did not go back inside.
“You come every day,” Nicolò said. “I see you. You take the cup out here as if the room were a prison.”
“The room is a room,” Elìa said. “The light is the rest of it.”
Nicolò looked at him the way a careful man looks at a crate with no mark on it. Then he laughed, which in him was not unkindness. It was the sound of a day that had decided to include one more thing.
“I’m roasting at San Barnaba,” he said. “If you insist on being cooked, you can be cooked where the coffee is better.”
That was the whole beginning. No destiny announced itself. Destiny, he had learned, was what you called a choice after the choice had already eaten twenty years.
They lived above the shop.
Two rooms and a window that faced a rio so narrow the opposite wall threw shade by ten, which meant Elìa opened the shutter at first light and stood in what the building would give him, and Nicolò complained that the sun would fade the sacks and the spines of the account books and the cheap print of the Madonna Nicolò’s sister had sent from Murano. Elìa opened the shutter anyway. Nicolò, after the first month, stopped taking the print down. He turned it to the wall at dawn and turned it back after the morning meal, and that small courtesy — the Madonna spared, the man fed — was the closest anyone in that century came to knowing what he was.
The shop smelled of roast and hemp and the sweet dust that coffee puts in the lines of a hand. Nicolò worked the way honest people work: as if the day were a tool you picked up and put down. Elìa translated for the warehouse until the warehouse no longer needed him, and then he translated for anyone who would pay a foreigner not to talk more than necessary. In the evenings they ate what the market at Campo Santa Margherita still had left — oil, a little fish, bread that had been good at noon. They slept in the heat. They woke when the bell of the Gesuati decided they should. They did not go to Carnival. The city performed itself in the piazzas and they let it. Happiness, it turned out, was a refusal. Two cups. A shutter. A man who said a name as if it were an ordinary word.
Nicolò said it Elìa, stressing the wrong place, making a Venetian thing of it. He did not correct him. He had been Raimond and other sounds besides. He had never liked a name so much as the one that came out of that mouth incorrectly.
The years did what years do when one of you is attached to the earth by a hook and the other is not.
Nicolò’s hair went at the temples. A seam came into the side of his smile and stayed. He began to take the stairs with a little noise in the knee. Elìa watched all of it the way a man watches weather on a house he loves and cannot keep. He did not age. He claimed, when Nicolò asked, the luck of a Levantine grandmother and the virtue of standing in the morning like a farmer. Nicolò believed him the way happy people believe a story that does not yet cost them anything. He would look across the table in the tenth year and the fifteenth and shake his head and say, “You are a theft. God will notice.”
God had already noticed. God, if that was the name for it, had noticed in another country, in another century, and had taken what it took, and had left him here with a flue in the chest and a debt to the light. Nicolò did not need to know that. Nicolò’s life was not a corridor that led to that door.
There were days — and he could still see them from the ferry, more clearly than he could see the last apartment — when the rio went high against the stones and the shop smelled of wet rope, and they sat on the bed with their feet up and counted the coins that would last until the water went down. Simple. That was the word he did not use at the time because he was inside it. Simple: a life that did not require a line or a map or a glass poured for anyone but the two of them. His work, in those rooms, ended at supper.
Love, he thought now, watching a white bird stitch the wake, is not a reason to stay.
People used it that way. They used it as glue and as argument and as the sentence they pronounced on someone else’s leaving. He had loved Nicolò enough to want the days to continue. That was not the same as having the right to continue them. Love, if it was going to be anything other than appetite wearing a better coat, was the discipline of letting a life be the shape it was. Nicolò’s life had a shape. It had a beginning in a parish he could still walk to. It had coffee and a sister on Murano and a knee that made a noise. It would have an end. The end was not an insult to the years above the shop. The end was how you knew they had been years.
For Nicolò, destiny was a road. It went somewhere. You could stand in the road with him and walk. You could not pick him up and put him into the weather another man had become.
That was the wound. Not the romance. The romance had been the happiest time of his life. The wound was that he did not get a road. He got mornings. He got east windows. He got the obligation to keep the earth fit to walk, which was a kind of love no one had asked him to feel and which would not, on its own, have kept him in two rooms in Dorsoduro for eighteen years. Nicolò had kept him. The work had waited. The work always waited. That was how you knew it was work.
In January of 1779 the fever came into the chest the way winter came into those rooms — without drama, as if it had always had a key.
Two weeks. Nicolò joked on the third day and did not joke on the tenth. The shop stayed shut. The sacks went stale. Elìa opened the shutter at dawn because his body required it and because the little winter sun of a Venetian January was the only thing in the city that still felt like a mercy, and he sat where Nicolò could see him and did not pretend the light was for both of them. It was not. The light would not go into another man’s lungs. That was not what it was for.
The draught was in the cupboard.
He had carried a turning bottle the way he carried languages: as a tool he hoped not to need. It wanted open sky. It wanted a recruit who would take it knowing what it cost. It wanted, above all, a soul already so hooked to the planet that heaven could tug and tug and not get the hook out. The old houses, when they were being clinical, called it trauma. A wound that had become a root. His own root was a courtyard he still did not enter — a door that had opened the wrong way, a name he did not say even in the languages that would have made it smaller, a family arranged on the stones in a pattern he had spent four hundred years not describing. That was why the draught had taken, in him, when it was offered. That was why he was sitting in a wet winter room in Dorsoduro instead of wherever ordinary men were allowed to go when the fever finished its work.
Nicolò had no such courtyard.
Nicolò had a sister who wrote in a round hand about the price of glass. He had a parish. He had an afterlife the way a man has a village over the next hill — not as a theory, as a place. Elìa had never been able to prove the geography of that place. He had only been able to refuse to steal it. The old rumor said vampires drank. The truth was cruder and more polite: they stayed. They stayed because something in them could not be received elsewhere. To pour the draught into a man who could still be received was not a rescue. It was a theft dressed as devotion.
He looked at the bottle on the ninth night, with the shutter cracked and a thin bar of morning on the floor, and Nicolò, who was not stupid, followed the look.
“Don’t,” Nicolò said. His voice was already a thing borrowed from farther away. “Whatever kindness you are inventing. I have been happy. That is a finished sentence. Do not open it again.”
He would not have taken it. Even if the sky and the flue and the ten names had been explained. Nicolò had the vanity of ordinary goodness: he wanted the road to end where it ended.
Elìa said, “All right.”
It was the only lie he did not have to tell. All right meant the bottle stayed in the dark. All right meant he would sit here and watch the shape leave the face he liked. All right meant he would not make an argument in a room that had never asked for one.
Nicolò died in the afternoon, which was a small courtesy. The bell of the Gesuati was doing something ordinary. The rio against the wall sounded like a rio. He held a wrist that had once pulled a sack out of his hands on the Zattere for no reason except July, and then there was no one in the wrist, and the planet — which would later require him to quiet cruel lines and walk out of apartments with the weight of other people’s endings — required nothing of him for an hour except that he stay in the chair.
He did not thank the sun that day. He thanked it the day after, because the body does not honor grief with fasting, and because Nicolò had turned the Madonna to the wall for him a thousand mornings and would have been irritated, in the old smiling way, to see him go gray at the mouth for theater.
He buried him where the parish pointed. He sold the sacks. He closed the shutter and left it closed. He put the bottle back among his names and went to another country, which is what his kind do when a life has finished being simple.
On the ferry a child dropped a plastic cup and the wind took it over the rail. The cup flashed once, a cheap lens, and then the ocean had it. Elias watched the place where it had been until the place was only water again.
The happiest time of his life had ended correctly. The correctness did not make it less happy. It also did not give it back.
What it gave him — and he could feel it now, with the Bahamas finally a faint interruption ahead, pale as a tooth — was a thin permission. Not a promise. He did not deal in those. A permission: that a life could be two rooms and a shutter and a mouth that said his name incorrectly, and that wanting that again was not a betrayal of the work. The work would find him. It always did. The eleventh name, if he was going to wear one long enough for a person to learn it, would have to include a table.
He did not know the table yet. He did not know the city. He knew the light on this water was a different color from the light on the rio — bluer, less like glass, more like a thing that had never had to negotiate with stone — and that his face, turned into it, still knew how to say thank you.
The engines changed their mind. The island came up the way islands do when you have been staring too long: suddenly, as if it had been pulled from under a cloth. White buildings. Green that did not exist in Dorsoduro. A dock with ropes that were the wrong color for Venice and the right color for here.
He stood. The sun hit the crown of his head and ran down.
Other passengers lifted bags. A woman laughed at a hat the wind wanted. The gangway knocked against the hull with a sound that was only itself.
Elias Ward — who could end at the next customs desk if he chose, and who had not yet chosen — put his hand on the rail and went down into the heat.
The boards of the dock were hot through the soles. Salt. Diesel. Someone calling a name that was not his. Ahead, a street that did not know him yet. Behind, a wake already forgetting the shape of the ferry.
He stepped off.
The past stayed on the water, intact, finished, shining. The future was only this: a different color of light, and the fact that he could still walk toward it.

These rather famous quotes from the 1940s supposedly by Elon are from world war 2 propaganda posters ...
(Wake Up/No Time for Sentiment/Never Know His Father/Loose Lips), the 1999 book title “Only the Paranoid Survive” by Andrew Grove about strategic inflection points, and a quote from a 1964 book & movie with Colin Firth “A Single Man”.

“Necessary for now” is part of a larger quote by CS Lewis about the future in his book, “Screwtape Letters”.

To be sure, the Enemy wants men to think of the Future too  - just so much as is NECESSARY FOR NOW planning the acts of justice or charity which will probably be their duty tomorrow. The duty of planning the morrow’s work is today’s duty; though its material is borrowed from the future, the duty, like all duties, is in the Present.… But we want a man hag-ridden by the Future.… We want a whole race perpetually in pursuit of the rainbow’s end, never honest, nor kind, nor happy now, but always using as mere fuel wherewith to heap the altar of the future every real gift which is offered them in the Present.”

It is unlike Elon or his personality to post this garbage.
